You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/maintenance (dev merged; quality 9.1 done; all prior modules complete). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite). This is the FINAL Phase 9 task; it completes Quality & Maintenance.

This OPENS the maintenance module (seventh business module). Scope per parity: equipment register + corrective + preventive (interval-based) maintenance orders. Functional locations, measurement points, maintenance notifications, and complex scheduling are OUT of v1.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md QM/PM section (PM v1 = "equipment register, corrective + preventive (interval-based) maintenance orders"; functional locations / measurement points / notifications = out of scope); docs/architecture.md D-012/D-013/D-014/D-015/D-022/D-025/D-007/D-029; DECISIONS D-032 (the background-job runner — a preventive-maintenance generation run that scans plans and creates due orders can be a job, but at v1 scale inline is fine — choose, mirroring the 6.4 reorder-scan inline decision). Then read the EXACT patterns to mirror:
- backend/app/modules/quality/ (the freshest small module: __init__/constants/models/schemas/service/queries/router, mounting) and backend/app/modules/manufacturing/ (a module with master + document + a periodic run); tests/modules/quality + tests/modules/manufacturing for fixtures.
- backend/app/core/{models.py (mixins, tenant_fk, tenant_unique, UuidPKMixin, MoneyType/QuantityType, DocumentMixin), rbac.py, conditional.py (ETag), pagination.py, numbering.py, deps.py}, core/jobs.py (if you make the preventive run a job).
- Cross-module (D-029, optional): a maintenance order MAY relate equipment to a finance cost center (opaque id validated via finance/queries.cost_center_exists) for cost attribution, and MAY consume spare-part items (opaque inventory ids) — but keep v1 LEAN: a maintenance order tracks labor/description/cost as a simple amount and optionally references a cost center; spare-parts stock issue is a documented later UNLESS trivial. Decide and document. Do NOT over-build — the parity scope is "equipment register + corrective/preventive orders," not full work-order costing.
Latest migration = 0035.

TASK — PLAN 9.2: maintenance — equipment register + corrective + preventive maintenance orders. Build:

1. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/__init__.py`, `constants.py`:
   - Enums: EquipmentStatus (ACTIVE|INACTIVE|RETIRED), MaintenanceOrderType (CORRECTIVE|PREVENTIVE), MaintenanceOrderStatus (DRAFT|SCHEDULED|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|CANCELLED), MaintenancePlanStatus (ACTIVE|INACTIVE), IntervalUnit (DAYS|WEEKS|MONTHS — the preventive interval).
   - Permissions: maintenance.equipment.read/.manage, maintenance.order.read/.manage/.complete, maintenance.plan.read/.manage, maintenance.plan.run (the generate-due-orders run).
   - Number sequences: 'maintenance.order' (MO-… conflicts with manufacturing order MO- — use 'WO-' work order or 'MNT-'; pick MNT- and document), equipment codes user-supplied unique per tenant.
   - Doc type + docflow links: maintenance-plan→maintenance-order (a preventive plan generates orders).
2. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/models.py` (or models/ if >400):
   - `Equipment` (`pm_equipment`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin; code (UNIQUE per tenant), name, description, status (EquipmentStatus), location (str — a free-text location label; NOT a functional-location hierarchy, that's out of v1), manufacturer/model/serial_number (str nullable), commissioned_date (Date nullable), cost_center_id (opaque finance cost-center id, nullable — validated via finance/queries if set), notes. tenant_unique().
   - `MaintenanceOrder` (`pm_maintenance_orders`): DocumentMixin header; order_number, order_type (CORRECTIVE|PREVENTIVE), status, equipment_id (composite tenant_fk to pm_equipment), maintenance_plan_id (nullable composite tenant_fk — set when generated by a preventive plan), description, scheduled_date (Date), completed_date (Date nullable), estimated_cost (MoneyType nullable), actual_cost (MoneyType nullable — recorded at completion), assigned_to (user id nullable), notes. A CORRECTIVE order is created ad-hoc; a PREVENTIVE order is generated by a plan. Index (tenant, equipment_id, status), (tenant, status, scheduled_date).
   - `MaintenancePlan` (`pm_maintenance_plans`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin; code (UNIQUE per tenant), name, equipment_id (composite tenant_fk), status (MaintenancePlanStatus), interval_value (int — every N), interval_unit (IntervalUnit), task_description, last_generated_date (Date nullable — the scheduled_date of the last order this plan generated), next_due_date (Date — computed: last_generated_date or a start date + interval), estimated_cost (MoneyType nullable). The plan defines a recurring preventive task; the generation run creates orders when next_due_date <= the run date.
3. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/schemas.py` (or schemas/): Create/Update/Read/Filter for Equipment, MaintenanceOrder, MaintenancePlan; action payloads (ScheduleOrder, CompleteOrder with actual_cost, RunPreventive).
4. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/service.py` (or service/ package, <400 each): 
   - equipment CRUD (code unique, cost_center exists if set, status transitions).
   - maintenance order: create_corrective (DRAFT/SCHEDULED, claim MNT number, equipment exists+ACTIVE), schedule (→ SCHEDULED), start (→ IN_PROGRESS), complete(order_id, actual_cost, completed_date) (→ COMPLETED, records actual_cost; optionally posts a maintenance-expense journal Dr maintenance-expense / Cr a clearing or accrual — DECIDE: v1 can record actual_cost on the order WITHOUT a GL posting (simplest, parity doesn't require PM→FI integration) OR post a simple expense journal via an event. Prefer: record cost on the order; a GL posting is a documented later UNLESS you want to wire it through the cost center — keep v1 lean and record-only, document clearly), cancel.
   - maintenance plan: CRUD (equipment exists, interval > 0, compute next_due_date), activate/deactivate.
   - `run_preventive_maintenance(session, tenant_id, as_of_date)` — scan ACTIVE plans whose next_due_date <= as_of_date, create a PREVENTIVE maintenance order per due plan (scheduled_date = next_due_date, linked docflow plan→order), advance the plan's last_generated_date = next_due_date and next_due_date += interval (handle a plan that's overdue by multiple intervals: generate ONE order and advance to the next future due date, OR generate one per missed interval — choose generate-one-and-advance-to-next-future, document; simplest + avoids order spam). Set-based scan (PERFORMANCE §2 — no per-plan N+1 beyond the order creation). Idempotent: running twice the same day doesn't double-generate (next_due_date advanced past as_of after the first run). Inline at v1 scale (document; a job is the later if plan counts grow).
   - idempotency on create/complete/run endpoints (D-013).
5. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/queries.py`: get_equipment, equipment_exists, get_maintenance_order, orders_for_equipment, get_maintenance_plan, due_plans(as_of). The only imported file.
6. `backend/app/modules/maintenance/router.py` (+ siblings if >400): equipment (CRUD, paginated+filter status+ETag), maintenance-orders (CRUD + schedule/start/complete/cancel; list paginated, filter equipment/type/status/date), maintenance-plans (CRUD + activate + a POST /maintenance-plans/run-preventive?as_of= that generates due orders). Permission-guard; mount in main.py. PERFORMANCE §6.
7. events.py/handlers.py only if you wire a GL posting on completion (if you keep it record-only, NO events — don't create empty files). Document the choice.
8. Migration 0036_maintenance.py (down_revision 0035): pm_equipment + pm_maintenance_orders + pm_maintenance_plans + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
9. docs/modules/maintenance.md: NEW module guide (equipment register, corrective vs preventive orders, the plan interval model + generation run + the overdue-advance rule, the v1 cost-recording (record-only or GL — whatever you chose), what's out of scope per parity). DECISIONS.md D-051 (maintenance scope: equipment + corrective/preventive orders; interval plan generation with generate-one-advance-to-next; v1 cost record-only vs GL decision).
10. Tests: test_equipment.py, test_maintenance_orders.py (create corrective, schedule/start/complete with actual_cost, equipment-must-be-active, lifecycle, cancel), test_maintenance_plans.py (CRUD, interval/next_due computation, run_preventive generates an order for a due plan + advances next_due, not-due plans skipped, idempotent re-run same day generates nothing, overdue-by-multiple advances to next future), test_maintenance_api.py (endpoints + RBAC + pagination + ≤3 budgets + ETag on equipment list + tenant isolation + the run-preventive endpoint). query_counter on lists + the run.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 9.2 (note Phase 9 / Quality & Maintenance COMPLETE) + DECISIONS.md D-051. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the equipment + order + plan model, the preventive-generation algorithm + overdue-advance rule + idempotency, the v1 cost-handling decision (record-only vs GL), test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

5:**Methodology.** All twelve functional areas below were verified through live web research against current sources (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting publications); no area was built from the embedded knowledge baseline alone. Five areas — Financial Accounting, Inventory Management & Warehousing, Quality Management & Plant Maintenance, Project System, and Cross-cutting platform concepts — supplemented web findings with embedded S/4HANA knowledge for specific subtopics or where source pages could not be fetched; these are flagged in the Sources appendix.
31:| Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM) | 1 | 4 | 7 | 12 |
125:In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), Sales covers the full order-to-cash cycle: business-partner-based customer master, condition-technique pricing, pre-sales documents and contracts, sales order processing, (advanced) available-to-promise with backorder processing, outbound delivery and goods issue, billing with FI integration, FSCM-based credit management, and Advanced Returns Management, plus condition contract settlement (rebates), output management, intercompany/third-party flows, and Fiori-based fulfillment monitoring. The Atlas v1 plan covers the essential transactional spine (quote → order → delivery → invoice with partial shipments, backorders, simple ATP, a credit-limit block, and RMA returns with credit notes) but deliberately simplifies the pricing engine, delivery execution, billing variants, and credit management, and omits contracts/scheduling agreements, output management, rebates, and intercompany/third-party processing.
133:| **Shipping and outbound deliveries** | Partial | sales | **Done (PLAN 7.3, the v1 scope):** `sales_deliveries`/`_lines` (DocumentMixin, `DN-` number, DRAFT→POSTED; created against a CONFIRMED/PARTIALLY_DELIVERED order with partial shipments + backorders = undelivered open lines) → on POST the goods issue runs via the event bus (`DeliveryShipped` → inventory ISSUE moves → finance **Dr COGS / Cr Inventory** at moving-average cost, COGS the default issue offset, D-045), `delivered_quantity` advances the order PARTIALLY_DELIVERED/DELIVERED, atomic + closed-period rollback, order→delivery→move docflow chain. No picking/packing/handling units, shipping point or route determination, wave processing, or warehouse/transportation integration. Later: Layer pick lists, packing/handling units, and shipping-point/route rules onto the delivery document later. |
165:## Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM)
167:In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), QM covers quality planning (inspection plans, master inspection characteristics, sampling), quality inspection (inspection lots auto-created at goods receipt, in production, and at delivery), characteristic-level results recording, coded usage decisions that drive stock postings out of quality-inspection stock, and quality notifications/CAPA, plus certificates and supplier quality. PM-EAM centers on technical objects (equipment installed on hierarchical functional locations), maintenance notifications feeding corrective maintenance orders with a phase-based lifecycle, preventive maintenance plans (time-, performance/counter-, and strategy-based) scheduled against task lists, and measurement points/counters for condition readings. Against the Atlas v1 plan, the GR-inspection-to-disposition flow, equipment register, and corrective/interval-based preventive orders cover a credible minimal core, but inspection plans, results recording, quality and maintenance notifications, functional locations, and measurement points are genuine gaps practitioners will notice.
175:| **Quality notifications (defects/complaints/CAPA)** | Out of scope | — | No defect/complaint workflow in v1; a rejected lot only moves stock and does not open a tracked quality issue. Later: Add a generic notification/issue object (shared with maintenance notifications) linkable to lots, suppliers, and materials. |
177:| **Equipment and functional locations (technical objects)** | Partial | maintenance | A flat equipment register is planned, but functional-location hierarchies, install/dismantle, and structure-based reporting are explicitly excluded. Later: Add a functional location entity with hierarchy codes and equipment installation/dismantle links. |
178:| **Maintenance notifications** | Out of scope | — | v1 creates corrective orders directly with no notification/request stage, losing breakdown reporting and MTBF/MTTR-style analysis. Later: Add a lightweight notification object convertible to an order, reusing the shared notification model. |
179:| **Corrective maintenance orders** | Full | maintenance | — |
180:| **Preventive maintenance plans and scheduling** | Partial | maintenance | Only fixed interval-based (time) preventive orders are planned; counter/performance-based and strategy plans are impossible without measurement points. Later: Once counters exist, extend the scheduler with performance-based cycles and packaged strategy plans. |
181:| **Measurement points and counters** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; no condition readings or counter-driven triggers are planned. Later: Add a measuring point entity on equipment with reading documents that feed maintenance plan scheduling. |
182:| **Maintenance task lists** | Out of scope | — | Not in the v1 plan; v1 preventive/corrective orders would carry free-text work instead of reusable standardized operations. Later: Add a task list master assignable to maintenance plan items and copyable into orders. |
271:SAP's S/4HANA industry approach folded most former IS add-ons into a single codebase ("industry to core"), covering roughly 25 industries whose functionality is activated per system through business function sets and the switch framework — activation is largely irreversible, one industry function set per instance, and industry-specific LoB functions are licensed separately from the Enterprise Management core. What the industry layer actually varies is substantial: terminology (Article vs Material, Site vs Plant), industry master data models (retail article/site, patient, equipment), entire vertical process suites (merchandise management, EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management, IS-U billing), regulatory content, and preconfigured SAP Best Practices content applied at setup. The current 2025/2026 direction adds a clean-core posture where deep vertical needs increasingly move to SAP Industry Cloud partner extensions on BTP — notably SAP is discontinuing healthcare IS-H by 2030 in favor of partner solutions. Atlas v1's YAML template layer maps well to the configuration-content slice of this area but plans none of the vertical process logic, industry master data objects, regulatory content, or partner extension ecosystem that practitioners associate with SAP industry solutions.

77	    item_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
78	    source: InspectionSource | None = None,
79	    cursor: str | None = None,
80	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
81	) -> Page[InspectionLot]:
82	    """Keyset-paginated inspection lots ordered by lot_number (D-014). The status/item/source
83	    filters
84	    narrow the set (index-served by (tenant, status) / (tenant, item_id)) and fold into the cursor
85	    fingerprint."""
86	    stmt = select(InspectionLot).where(InspectionLot.tenant_id == tenant_id)
87	    if status is not None:
88	        stmt = stmt.where(InspectionLot.status == status.value)
89	    if item_id is not None:
90	        stmt = stmt.where(InspectionLot.item_id == item_id)
91	    if source is not None:
92	        stmt = stmt.where(InspectionLot.source == source.value)
93	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(status, item_id, source)
94	    return await paginate(
95	        session,
96	        stmt,
97	        order_by=[OrderKey(InspectionLot.lot_number, SortDirection.ASC)],
98	        pk=InspectionLot.id,
99	        cursor=cursor,
100	        limit=limit,
101	        filters=fingerprint,
102	    )

105	async def create_lot_from_receipt_line(
106	    session: AsyncSession,
107	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
108	    *,
109	    source_document_id: uuid.UUID,
110	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
111	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,

118	    """Create one OPEN inspection lot for a flagged GR line (D-050) — called by the GR handler in
119	    the
120	    GR post's transaction. Registers the document, claims the gapless QL- number (a permanent
121	    document at creation, the orders/receipts branch), and snapshots the GR line's item/bin/qty/
122	    tracked-instance. The docflow GR→lot edge is written by the caller (the handler)."""

142	    )
143	    lot = InspectionLot(

173	def _validate_decision_split(lot: InspectionLot, payload: InspectionDecideRequest) -> None:
174	    """The accept/reject split must be non-negative and sum to EXACTLY the lot quantity (v1: one
175	    decision covers the whole lot)."""
176	    accepted = Decimal(str(payload.accepted_quantity))
177	    rejected = Decimal(str(payload.rejected_quantity))
178	    if accepted < 0 or rejected < 0:
179	        raise ValidationFailedError(
180	            message="Accepted and rejected quantities must be non-negative",
181	            code="quality.decision_quantity_invalid",
182	        )
183	    if accepted + rejected != Decimal(str(lot.quantity)):
184	        raise ValidationFailedError(
185	            message="Accepted plus rejected quantity must equal the lot quantity",
186	            code="quality.decision_quantity_mismatch",
187	            details={
188	                "lot_quantity": str(lot.quantity),
189	                "accepted_quantity": str(accepted),
190	                "rejected_quantity": str(rejected),
191	            },
192	        )

194	
195	async def _validate_disposition(
196	    session: AsyncSession,
197	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
198	    payload: InspectionDecideRequest,
199	) -> RejectDisposition:
200	    """A reject (rejected > 0) requires an IMPLEMENTED disposition; a BLOCK requires a valid
201	    destination bin. Returns the validated disposition."""
202	    if payload.disposition is None:
203	        raise ValidationFailedError(
204	            message="A rejection requires a disposition",
205	            code="quality.disposition_required",
206	        )
207	    disposition = RejectDisposition(payload.disposition)
208	    if disposition == RejectDisposition.RETURN_TO_VENDOR:
209	        raise ValidationFailedError(
210	            message="RETURN_TO_VENDOR disposition is not implemented in v1",
211	            code="quality.disposition_not_implemented",
212	            details={"disposition": disposition.value},
213	        )
214	    if disposition == RejectDisposition.BLOCK:
215	        if payload.blocked_bin_id is None:
216	            raise ValidationFailedError(
217	                message="A BLOCK disposition requires a destination blocked bin",
218	                code="quality.blocked_bin_required",
219	            )
220	        if not await inventory_queries.bin_exists(
221	            session, tenant_id, payload.blocked_bin_id
222	        ):
223	            raise ValidationFailedError(
224	                message="The blocked bin does not exist",
225	                code="quality.blocked_bin_not_found",
226	                details={"bin_id": str(payload.blocked_bin_id)},
227	            )
228	    return disposition
229	
230	
231	async def decide(
232	    session: AsyncSession,
233	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
234	    lot_id: uuid.UUID,
235	    payload: InspectionDecideRequest,
236	    *,
237	    decision_by: uuid.UUID,
238	    decided_date: date | None = None,
239	) -> InspectionLot:
240	    """The usage DECISION (D-050) — accept/reject the lot. Validates the accept/reject split sums to
241	    the lot quantity; when rejected > 0 requires a disposition and PUBLISHES
242	    ``InspectionDispositioned`` so inventory moves the rejected stock (SCRAP = an ADJUSTMENT-out
243	    write-off; BLOCK = a TRANSFER to the blocked bin). Sets ACCEPTED (rejected == 0) or REJECTED
244	    (rejected > 0) with both quantities recorded; stamps decided_date/by. ACCEPTED needs NO stock
245	    move — the accepted stock is already on hand and usable. Idempotent: a decided lot is terminal
246	    (re-decide → 409). Atomic — a SCRAP write-off into a CLOSED period rolls the whole decision
247	    back.
248	    The caller commits via uow; the published event drains in that same uow."""
249	    lot = await get_inspection_lot(session, tenant_id, lot_id)
250	    if InspectionLotStatus(lot.status) != InspectionLotStatus.OPEN:
251	        raise ConflictError(
252	            message=f"A {lot.status} inspection lot cannot be decided",
253	            code="quality.lot_not_open",
254	            details={"lot_id": str(lot_id), "status": lot.status},
255	        )
256	
257	    _validate_decision_split(lot, payload)
258	    accepted = Decimal(str(payload.accepted_quantity))
259	    rejected = Decimal(str(payload.rejected_quantity))
260	
261	    disposition: RejectDisposition | None = None
262	    if rejected > 0:
263	        disposition = await _validate_disposition(session, tenant_id, payload)
264	
265	    move_date = decided_date or date.today()
266	    lot.accepted_quantity = accepted
267	    lot.rejected_quantity = rejected
268	    lot.disposition = disposition.value if disposition is not None else None
269	    lot.decided_date = move_date
270	    lot.decision_by = decision_by
271	    new_status = (
272	        InspectionLotStatus.ACCEPTED if rejected == 0 else InspectionLotStatus.REJECTED
273	    )
274	    lot.status = new_status.value
275	    await session.flush()
276	    await docflow.set_document_status(
277	        session, tenant_id, lot.document_id, status=new_status.value
278	    )
279	
280	    # Only a REJECT moves stock — publish AFTER the lot's own writes settle so inventory's handler
281	    # creates the disposition move (and, for SCRAP, the write-off journal) in this same uow (D-011).
282	    if rejected > 0 and disposition is not None:
283	        publish(
284	            session,
285	            InspectionDispositioned(
286	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
287	                lot_id=lot.id,
288	                lot_number=lot.lot_number,
289	                document_id=lot.document_id,
290	                disposition=disposition.value,
291	                item_id=lot.item_id,
292	                rejected_quantity=rejected,
293	                from_bin_id=lot.bin_id,
294	                to_bin_id=(
295	                    payload.blocked_bin_id
296	                    if disposition == RejectDisposition.BLOCK
297	                    else None
298	                ),
299	                inventory_lot_id=lot.inspect_lot_id,
300	                serial_id=lot.serial_id,
301	                move_date=move_date.isoformat(),
302	            ),
303	        )
304	    return lot
305	
306	
307	async def cancel_lot(
308	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, lot_id: uuid.UUID
309	) -> InspectionLot:
310	    """Cancel an OPEN inspection lot (D-050) — a flagged GR posted in error, the lot is moot. A
311	    decided (ACCEPTED/REJECTED) lot is terminal and cannot be cancelled. Moves no stock."""
312	    lot = await get_inspection_lot(session, tenant_id, lot_id)
313	    if InspectionLotStatus(lot.status) != InspectionLotStatus.OPEN:
314	        raise ConflictError(
315	            message=f"A {lot.status} inspection lot cannot be cancelled",
316	            code="quality.lot_not_cancellable",
317	            details={"lot_id": str(lot_id), "status": lot.status},
318	        )
319	    lot.status = InspectionLotStatus.CANCELLED.value
320	    await session.flush()
321	    await docflow.set_document_status(
322	        session, tenant_id, lot.document_id, status=InspectionLotStatus.CANCELLED.value
323	    )
324	    return lot
325

4	decision

6	auto-creates an OPEN lot). Every route is guarded by a quality permission key (D-009); writes commit
7	through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so the decision + its disposition stock move + write-off journal +
8	audit rows ride the SAME transaction. The decision is IDEMPOTENT (D-013). The list is O(1) queries +
9	paginated (PERFORMANCE §6).

1	"""Declarative Base with the D-022 naming convention and shared model mixins."""
2	
3	import uuid
4	from datetime import UTC, datetime
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import sqlalchemy as sa
8	from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
9	from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
10	
11	# Deterministic constraint names are mandatory: SQLite batch-mode migrations
12	# cannot drop unnamed constraints (D-022).
13	NAMING_CONVENTION = {
14	    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
15	    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
16	    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
17	    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
18	    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
19	}
20	
21	# Portable JSON: JSONB on Postgres, plain JSON elsewhere. Type variance lives in
22	# the models so migrations import it from here and stay dialect-clean (D-022).
23	JSON_VARIANT = sa.JSON().with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), "postgresql")
24	
25	
26	class Base(DeclarativeBase):
27	    metadata = sa.MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)
28	
29	
30	class UuidPKMixin:
31	    """uuid4 primary key, client-generated so ids are portable across both engines."""
32	
33	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
34	
35	
36	class TenantMixin:
37	    """Row-level tenancy marker (D-007). Filtering and stamping are enforced by the
38	    core/tenancy.py session listeners; query authors never touch tenant_id."""
39	
40	    @declared_attr
41	    def tenant_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
42	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, index=True)
43	
44	
45	class AuditMixin:
46	    """Marker mixin (D-010): tags a model for split-phase audit capture. It adds NO
47	    columns — the audit listeners in core/audit.py test ``isinstance(obj, AuditMixin)``
48	    to decide which INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE flushes land in core_audit_log. Per-column
49	    opt-outs are declared on the model via ``__audit_exclude__`` (a frozenset of
50	    attribute names); ``password_hash`` is excluded there on User."""
51	
52	    # Attribute names never written to the diff (D-010: password_hash always). Models
53	    # override by setting their own frozenset; the listeners read it via getattr.
54	    __audit_exclude__: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
55	
56	
57	def utcnow() -> datetime:
58	    """Canonical timestamp source for every SQLAlchemy write (#34)."""
59	    return datetime.now(UTC)
60	
61	
62	class TimestampMixin:
63	    """Timezone-aware UTC stamps, ALWAYS Python-written (#34).
64	
65	    The Python ``default``/``onupdate`` fire for ORM and Core inserts alike, so every
66	    stored value uses SQLAlchemy's canonical SQLite string format (six-digit
67	    microseconds). The DDL ``server_default`` remains only as a fallback for raw SQL
68	    outside SQLAlchemy and must never be relied on: SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes
69	    second-precision strings whose lexicographic comparison against bound datetimes
70	    breaks keyset-pagination equality — the #34 infinite-page-loop bug."""
71	
72	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
73	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
74	        nullable=False,
75	        default=utcnow,
76	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
77	    )
78	    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
79	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
80	        nullable=False,

1	"""Work-centre business logic (PLAN 8.1): CRUD + cost-centre validation.
2	
3	The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin. The optional
4	``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id (D-029): validated to exist via
5	``finance/queries.cost_center_exists`` (the sanctioned cross-module read, STRUCTURE §5) — never a
6	cross-module FK. ``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[WorkCenter]`` (the ORM model) a
7	string at import; the router re-validates page items.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
18	from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
19	from app.core.schemas import Page
20	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
21	from app.modules.manufacturing.models import WorkCenter
22	from app.modules.manufacturing.schemas import (
23	    WorkCenterCreate,
24	    WorkCenterFilter,
25	    WorkCenterUpdate,
26	)
27	
28	
29	async def _validate_cost_center(
30	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None
31	) -> None:
32	    """A supplied cost-centre id must exist in finance (D-029): validated via the finance queries
33	    contract, never a cross-module FK. None is skipped (the cost centre is optional)."""
34	    if cost_center_id is None:
35	        return
36	    if not await finance_queries.cost_center_exists(session, tenant_id, cost_center_id):
37	        raise ValidationFailedError(
38	            message="Referenced cost centre does not exist",
39	            code="manufacturing.cost_center_not_found",
40	            details={"cost_center_id": str(cost_center_id)},
41	        )
42	
43	
44	async def get_work_center(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, work_center_id: uuid.UUID
46	) -> WorkCenter:
47	    work_center = await session.get(WorkCenter, work_center_id)
48	    if work_center is None or work_center.tenant_id != tenant_id:
49	        raise NotFoundError(
50	            message="Work centre not found", code="manufacturing.work_center_not_found"
51	        )
52	    return work_center
53	
54	
55	async def create_work_center(
56	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: WorkCenterCreate
57	) -> WorkCenter:
58	    """Create a work centre. Rejects a duplicate code (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop); validates the
59	    cost centre exists in finance when set."""
60	    existing = (
61	        await session.execute(
62	            select(WorkCenter.id).where(
63	                WorkCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id, WorkCenter.code == payload.code
64	            )
65	        )
66	    ).first()
67	    if existing is not None:
68	        raise ConflictError(
69	            message=f"A work centre with code {payload.code} already exists",
70	            code="manufacturing.work_center_code_conflict",
71	            details={"code": payload.code},
72	        )
73	    await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, payload.cost_center_id)
74	    work_center = WorkCenter(
75	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
76	        code=payload.code,
77	        name=payload.name,
78	        description=payload.description,
79	        cost_center_id=payload.cost_center_id,
80	        capacity_hours_per_day=payload.capacity_hours_per_day,
81	        efficiency_percent=payload.efficiency_percent,
82	        is_active=payload.is_active,
83	    )
84	    session.add(work_center)
85	    await session.flush()
86	    return work_center
87	
88	
89	async def update_work_center(
90	    session: AsyncSession,
91	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
92	    work_center_id: uuid.UUID,
93	    payload: WorkCenterUpdate,
94	) -> WorkCenter:
95	    """Partial update (D-010: mutate the loaded object so the audit diff is captured). ``code`` is
96	    immutable and absent from the schema; a changed cost centre is re-validated."""
97	    work_center = await get_work_center(session, tenant_id, work_center_id)
98	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
99	    if "cost_center_id" in data:
100	        await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, data["cost_center_id"])
101	    for field, value in data.items():
102	        setattr(work_center, field, value)
103	    await session.flush()
104	    return work_center
105	
106	
107	async def list_work_centers(
108	    session: AsyncSession,
109	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
110	    *,
111	    filters: WorkCenterFilter,
112	    cursor: str | None = None,
113	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
114	) -> Page[WorkCenter]:
115	    """Keyset-paginated work centres ordered by code (D-014). The active filter narrows the set and
116	    folds into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot bleed across views."""
117	    stmt = select(WorkCenter).where(WorkCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id)
118	    if filters.is_active is not None:
119	        stmt = stmt.where(WorkCenter.is_active == filters.is_active)
120	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(filters.is_active)
121	    return await paginate(
122	        session,
123	        stmt,
124	        order_by=[OrderKey(WorkCenter.code, SortDirection.ASC)],
125	        pk=WorkCenter.id,
126	        cursor=cursor,
127	        limit=limit,
128	        filters=fingerprint,
129	    )

10	``sa.Numeric`` would round-trip through float on SQLite and lose precision (D-015), so it is never

39	    is later), validated to exist in finance when set — no cross-module FK. Audited (D-010): master

1	"""Manufacturing constants (STRUCTURE §3): the BOM/routing status enums and the permission keys,
2	registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap, the
5	inventory precedent) — PLAN 8.1's masters sit well under that. Production orders (8.2) and MRP (8.3)
6	will add their own document types / number sequences / event keys; if that pushes this past the cap
7	it becomes a constants/ package then, the sales precedent.
8	
9	IDENTITY + NUMBERING (decided here, D-047). Manufacturing MASTERS carry no gapless document number:
10	
11	- **Work centres** and the BOM/routing CODE-bearing identity follow the master-data precedent
12	  (item_code / vendor_code / customer_code): ``work_center_code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per
13	  tenant (``UNIQUE(tenant_id, code)``). A code, not a gapless number.
14	- **A BOM is identified by ``(item_id, version)``** — the item it PRODUCES plus a user-supplied
15	  version string — NOT a standalone code, mirroring S/4HANA's "BOM is keyed by material + BOM
16	  usage/alternative". ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_id, version)``. The same shape is used for routings
17	  for consistency: a routing is ``(item_id, version)`` too (NOT a routing_code), so BOM and routing
18	  identity read identically and a routing can be looked up the same way a BOM is.
19	
20	There is deliberately NO auto-sequence here: a master carries a stable user-chosen handle, never a
21	gapless number. The PRODUCTION ORDERS in 8.2 WILL register documents and claim a gapless number (a
22	posted document in the D-012 sense) — but the masters do not.
23	
24	ACTIVATION MODEL (D-047). A BOM/routing version has a lifecycle status (DRAFT|ACTIVE|INACTIVE):
25	
26	- **DRAFT** — editable: components/operations may be added, changed and removed. A new version is
27	  born DRAFT.
28	- **ACTIVE** — usable by production/MRP and FROZEN: its components/operations can no longer be
29	  changed (corrections are a NEW version, the append-only-master philosophy). At most ONE
30	  ACTIVE+``is_default`` version per item — the one ``get_active_bom_for_item`` /

50	class ProductionOrderStatus(StrEnum):
51	    """Lifecycle of a PRODUCTION ORDER (PLAN 8.2, D-048). A production order turns components into a
52	    finished parent item; its status tracks the issue→finish progress.
53	
54	    Transitions (the service owns them, CLAUDE.md rule 7):
55	
56	    - **DRAFT** — created + the active BOM EXPLODED into reserved component rows (and the routing
57	      snapshotted into order operations). Editable only via cancel; releasing moves it forward.
58	    - **RELEASED** — materials are reserved (the component rows ARE the reservation, v1 ATP-style —
59	      release does NOT block on availability, only optionally flags shortages). Ready to issue.
60	    - **IN_PROGRESS** — at least one component has been issued to WIP (Dr WIP / Cr Inventory). The
61	      order is mid-production: it can issue more components or finish.
62	    - **FINISHED** — the parent item has been fully produced to stock (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP) and
63	      the ordered quantity is met. Terminal; WIP nets to zero (issue debits = finished credit +
64	      variance flush).
65	    - **CANCELLED** — abandoned before any component issued (DRAFT/RELEASED only). Once components
66	      are issued the order is POSTED-ish: it must be FINISHED (a future phase adds reversal), never
67	      cancelled, so issued stock + WIP never strand. Terminal.
68	    """
69	
70	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
71	    RELEASED = "RELEASED"
72	    IN_PROGRESS = "IN_PROGRESS"
73	    FINISHED = "FINISHED"
74	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"

2	component reservations, and the routing-snapshot operations.
3	
4	A production order turns COMPONENTS into a FINISHED parent item: a header (``ProductionOrder``) plus
5	its ``ProductionOrderComponent`` rows (the BOM exploded at create time — required vs issued
6	quantity) and its ``ProductionOrderOperation`` rows (the routing snapshotted for 8.3's capacity
7	load). The header mixes in ``DocumentMixin`` (it registers in core_documents + claims an MO- number
8	at creation — a posted document, unlike the 8.1 masters).
9

11	tables; the service validates each via ``inventory/queries`` before writing. The ``bom_id``/
12	``routing_id`` are INTRA-module composite tenant FKs to ``mfg_boms``/``mfg_routings`` (the exploded
13	version snapshots). Quantities use the D-015 QuantityType (scale-6, exact on both engines);
14	``accumulated_wip_cost`` uses MoneyType (the value side, quantized to currency).
15	
16	``accumulated_wip_cost`` is the running WIP debit for this order: raised by each component issue (by
17	the posted issue cost) and consumed at finish to compute the finished unit cost — the SSOT for the
18	WIP-nets-to-zero invariant (D-048), maintained on the header rather than recomputed from the journal

187	async def register_document(

225	) -> None:
226	    """Update a registry row's status and/or doc_number in the owning transaction (D-012).
227	
228	    The number is assigned at the moment a draft-lifecycle document becomes permanent (journal
229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
234	    values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
235	    if status is not None:
236	        values["status"] = status
237	    if doc_number is not None:
238	        values["doc_number"] = doc_number

240	        return

242	        sa.update(Document.__table__)
243	        .where(

245	            Document.__table__.c.id == document_id,
246	        )
247	        .values(**values)

251	async def link_documents(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    predecessor: uuid.UUID,
255	    successor: uuid.UUID,
256	    link_type: str | None = None,
257	) -> DocumentLink:
258	    """Create a predecessor -> successor edge and return it (D-012). The UNIQUE(tenant_id,
259	    predecessor, successor) constraint rejects a duplicate edge as an IntegrityError, and
260	    the composite tenant FKs reject endpoints from another tenant. A Core insert sets
261	    tenant_id explicitly (D-007 sanctioned site)."""
262	    link_id = uuid.uuid4()
263	    await session.execute(
264	        sa.insert(DocumentLink.__table__).values(
265	            id=link_id,
266	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
267	            predecessor_document_id=predecessor,
268	            successor_document_id=successor,
269	            link_type=link_type,
270	        )
271	    )
272	    return (
273	        await session.execute(select(DocumentLink).where(DocumentLink.id == link_id))
274	    ).scalar_one()

276	
277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320	
321	
322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,
378	            successor_document_id=link.successor_document_id,
379	            link_type=link.link_type,
380	        )
381	        for link in link_rows
382	    ]
383	
384	    return DocumentChain(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)

1	"""The MRP run engine (PLAN 8.3, D-049, parity PP MRP = PARTIAL): the deterministic, set-based,
2	level-ordered planning pass that nets demand against supply and writes planned orders.
3	
4	THE MODEL (D-049):
5	
6	- **Demand** per item = open sales-order demand (Σ ordered − delivered over CONFIRMED /
7	  PARTIALLY_DELIVERED sales orders, via ``sales/queries.committed_quantity``) + reorder-point
8	  shortfall (an item at/below its reorder point demands ``reorder_quantity``, via
9	  ``inventory/queries.items_below_reorder_point``). These are the LEVEL-0 (independent) demands.
10	- **Supply** per item = on-hand (``inventory/queries.total_on_hand``) + un-finished open production
11	  orders (``manufacturing/queries.open_production_order_supply``) + open-incoming POs
12	  (``procurement/queries.open_incoming_quantity``) + still-open FIRMED/CONVERTED planned orders
13	  (``manufacturing/queries.planned_make_supply`` — the regeneration policy keeps committed
14	  proposals as supply).
15	- **Net requirement** = max(0, demand − supply).
16	- **MAKE vs BUY** is STRUCTURAL: an item with an ACTIVE default BOM is MAKE (produced in-house, its
17	  BOM is EXPLODED into dependent component demand); an item with no active BOM is BUY (a leaf the
18	  explosion stops at — a planned BUY order).
19	- **The explosion is LEVEL-ORDERED**: level 0 (independently-demanded items) is netted first; each
20	  MAKE item's net requirement EXPLODES its BOM into dependent demand for its components at the next
21	  level, accumulating across all parents (a component used by two finished goods sums). Each level
22	  is processed set-based (the level's items' BOMs/components are batched), capped at
23	  ``MRP_MAX_EXPLOSION_LEVELS`` so a (masters-rejected-but-defensive) cycle terminates.
24	
25	BULK / SET-BASED (PERFORMANCE §2): per level the engine issues a BOUNDED number of queries — it
26	batches the level's active BOMs (ONE query), their components (ONE query), then per item resolves
27	demand/supply through the cross-module queries (each item-level read is one query, but the NUMBER of
28	levels is capped and the per-item cross-module reads are the same shape the ATP/reorder paths use —
29	no per-component N+1 inside a level's explosion). The planned orders are written with ONE bulk
30	insert; the run header + regeneration delete are O(1).
31	
32	EXECUTION (PERFORMANCE §3, D-049): the run scans every planning-relevant item, so it is ALWAYS a
33	``manufacturing.mrp_run`` BACKGROUND JOB — the endpoint submits the job and returns 202 {job_id};
34	the handler here calls :func:`run_mrp`. The rough capacity check (``mrp_capacity.py``) runs as part
35	of the same job after the plan is written.
36	
37	Conversion (firm/convert/cancel) + the run/planned-order reads live in ``planned_orders.py``; the
38	capacity check in ``mrp_capacity.py``. ``service/__init__`` re-exports all three.
39	"""

86	    item_id: uuid.UUID
87	    order_type: str
88	    quantity: Decimal
89	    level: int
90	    source_notes: str
91	
92	
93	async def _gather_independent_demand(
94	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
95	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
96	    """Level-0 (independent) demand per item: open sales-order demand + reorder-point shortfall
97	    (module docstring). Returns ``{item_id: total_demand}``. Two set-based reads (the reorder scan +
98	    the open-sales-demand items) plus one ``committed_quantity`` per demanded item — the same shape
99	    sales ATP uses, no per-line N+1 inside."""
100	    demand: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
101	
102	    # Reorder-point shortfall: each below-reorder item demands its reorder_quantity (the 6.4 scan's
103	    # source) — ONE set-based query.
104	    below = await inventory_queries.items_below_reorder_point(session, tenant_id)
105	    for item_id, _on_hand, _rp, reorder_quantity in below:
106	        demand[item_id] = demand.get(item_id, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(str(reorder_quantity))
107	
108	    # Open sales-order demand: the items with undelivered confirmed sales-order lines, each summed
109	    # via committed_quantity (the ATP reservation source). One query to find the items, then the
110	    # committed sum per item (the sales-module-owned read).
111	    for item_id, qty in (await _open_sales_demand_items(session, tenant_id)).items():
112	        demand[item_id] = demand.get(item_id, Decimal(0)) + qty
113	    return demand
114	
115	
116	async def _open_sales_demand_items(
117	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
118	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
119	    """The items carrying open sales-order demand + the committed quantity per item (PLAN 8.3).
120	    Reads the SALES module: first the distinct items on undelivered confirmed order lines (one
121	    query through sales/queries), then ``committed_quantity`` per item (the canonical reservation
122	    sum). Bounded: one discovery query + one committed read per demanded item (the small set)."""
123	    item_ids = await sales_queries.open_demand_item_ids(session, tenant_id)
124	    result: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
125	    for item_id in item_ids:
126	        qty = await sales_queries.committed_quantity(session, tenant_id, item_id)
127	        if qty > 0:
128	            result[item_id] = qty
129	    return result
130	
131	
132	async def _net_supply(
133	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
134	) -> Decimal:
135	    """The total SUPPLY of an item (module docstring): on-hand + un-finished open production
136	    orders + open-incoming POs + still-open FIRMED/CONVERTED planned orders. Four bounded
137	    cross-module reads (no N+1), summed exact (D-015)."""
138	    on_hand = Decimal(str(await inventory_queries.total_on_hand(session, tenant_id, item_id)))
139	    production = await mfg_queries.open_production_order_supply(session, tenant_id, item_id)
140	    on_order = Decimal(
141	        str(await procurement_queries.open_incoming_quantity(session, tenant_id, item_id))
142	    )
143	    firmed = await mfg_queries.planned_make_supply(session, tenant_id, item_id)
144	    return on_hand + production + on_order + firmed
145	
146	
147	async def _active_boms_for(
148	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_ids: list[uuid.UUID]
149	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Bom]:
150	    """The ACTIVE default BOMs for a BATCH of items (PLAN 8.3) — ONE query (the level's MAKE-vs-BUY
151	    test + explosion input), keyed by item_id. An item absent from the result is BUY (no active
152	    BOM)."""
153	    if not item_ids:
154	        return {}
155	    stmt = select(Bom).where(
156	        Bom.tenant_id == tenant_id,
157	        Bom.item_id.in_(item_ids),
158	        Bom.status == BomStatus.ACTIVE.value,
159	        Bom.is_default.is_(True),
160	    )
161	    return {bom.item_id: bom for bom in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all()}
162	
163	
164	async def _components_for(
165	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bom_ids: list[uuid.UUID]
166	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, list[BomComponent]]:
167	    """The components of a BATCH of BOMs (PLAN 8.3) — ONE query, grouped by bom_id (the level's
168	    explosion input, no per-BOM N+1)."""
169	    if not bom_ids:
170	        return {}
171	    stmt = (
172	        select(BomComponent)
173	        .where(BomComponent.tenant_id == tenant_id, BomComponent.bom_id.in_(bom_ids))
174	        .order_by(BomComponent.line_number)
175	    )
176	    grouped: dict[uuid.UUID, list[BomComponent]] = {}
177	    for component in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all():
178	        grouped.setdefault(component.bom_id, []).append(component)
179	    return grouped
180	
181	
182	def _explode(
183	    bom: Bom, components: list[BomComponent], parent_net: Decimal
184	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
185	    """Dependent component demand from making ``parent_net`` units of a BOM's parent (PLAN 8.3):
186	    per component, ``quantity_per × parent_net / base_quantity × (1 + scrap_percent/100)``,
187	    quantized — the create_production_order explosion math. Returns
188	    ``{component_item_id: dependent_demand}`` (summed when a component repeats)."""
189	    base_quantity = Decimal(str(bom.base_quantity))
190	    out: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
191	    for component in components:
192	        scrap_factor = Decimal(1) + (Decimal(str(component.scrap_percent)) / Decimal(100))
193	        dependent = _quantize_qty(
194	            (Decimal(str(component.quantity_per)) * parent_net / base_quantity) * scrap_factor
195	        )
196	        if dependent > 0:
197	            out[component.component_item_id] = out.get(
198	                component.component_item_id, Decimal(0)
199	            ) + dependent
200	    return out
201	
202	
203	async def _plan_levels(
204	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
205	) -> list[_PlanLine]:
206	    """Net demand against supply LEVEL BY LEVEL, exploding MAKE items (module docstring). Returns
207	    the accumulated planned-order lines. Level 0 is the independent demand; each subsequent level
208	    is the dependent demand the prior level's MAKE explosions raised, capped at
209	    ``MRP_MAX_EXPLOSION_LEVELS`` (cycle guard). Per level the BOM lookups are batched (two
210	    queries); the per-item demand/supply reads reuse the bounded cross-module queries (no N+1)."""
211	    lines: list[_PlanLine] = []
212	    # The current level's GROSS demand per item (independent at level 0, dependent thereafter).
213	    pending: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = await _gather_independent_demand(session, tenant_id)
214	    # Items already netted in an EARLIER level — the cycle/diamond guard: a component re-appearing
215	    # at a deeper level is folded into its earlier net rather than re-planned (low-level-code).
216	    netted: set[uuid.UUID] = set()
217	    level = 0
218	
219	    while pending and level < MRP_MAX_EXPLOSION_LEVELS:
220	        item_ids = [item_id for item_id in pending if item_id not in netted]
221	        if not item_ids:
222	            break
223	        boms = await _active_boms_for(session, tenant_id, item_ids)
224	        components_by_bom = await _components_for(
225	            session, tenant_id, [bom.id for bom in boms.values()]
226	        )
227	        next_pending: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
228	        for item_id in item_ids:
229	            gross = pending[item_id]
230	            supply = await _net_supply(session, tenant_id, item_id)
231	            net = gross - supply
232	            netted.add(item_id)
233	            if net <= 0:
234	                continue  # supply covers it — no planned order, no dependent demand
235	            net = _quantize_qty(net)
236	            bom = boms.get(item_id)
237	            order_type = (
238	                PlannedOrderType.MAKE.value if bom is not None else PlannedOrderType.BUY.value
239	            )
240	            lines.append(
241	                _PlanLine(
242	                    item_id=item_id,
243	                    order_type=order_type,
244	                    quantity=net,
245	                    level=level,
246	                    source_notes=f"net {net} = demand {_quantize_qty(gross)} - supply "
247	                    f"{_quantize_qty(supply)}",
248	                )
249	            )
250	            if bom is not None:
251	                for component_id, dependent in _explode(
252	                    bom, components_by_bom.get(bom.id, []), net
253	                ).items():
254	                    next_pending[component_id] = (
255	                        next_pending.get(component_id, Decimal(0)) + dependent
256	                    )
257	        pending = next_pending
258	        level += 1
259	    return lines
260	
261	
262	async def _regenerate(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
263	    """Delete the tenant's prior PLANNED (un-firmed) planned orders before writing a fresh plan (the
264	    regeneration policy, D-049): a re-run supersedes un-committed proposals. FIRMED / CONVERTED /
265	    CANCELLED rows survive (FIRMED/CONVERTED net as supply via ``planned_make_supply``). ONE
266	    set-based DELETE."""
267	    await session.execute(
268	        delete(PlannedOrder).where(
269	            PlannedOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
270	            PlannedOrder.status == PlannedOrderStatus.PLANNED.value,
271	        )
272	    )
273	
274	
275	async def _create_run(
276	    session: AsyncSession,
277	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
278	    run_date: date,
279	    horizon_days: int,
280	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None,
281	) -> MrpRun:
282	    """Register the run document, claim its gapless MRP- number, persist the RUNNING run row (D-012,
283	    the depreciation-run precedent)."""
284	    run_id = uuid.uuid4()
285	    document = await docflow.register_document(
286	        session,
287	        tenant_id,
288	        MRP_RUN_DOC_TYPE,
289	        run_id,
290	        doc_number=None,
291	        status=MrpRunStatus.RUNNING.value,
292	    )
293	    await ensure_sequence(
294	        session,
295	        tenant_id,
296	        MRP_RUN_SEQUENCE_NAME,
297	        MRP_RUN_NUMBER_PREFIX,
298	        MRP_RUN_NUMBER_PADDING,
299	        year_reset=True,
300	    )
301	    run_number = await claim_number(session, tenant_id, MRP_RUN_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=run_date)
302	    run = MrpRun(
303	        id=run_id,
304	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
305	        document_id=document.id,
306	        run_number=run_number,
307	        status=MrpRunStatus.RUNNING.value,
308	        run_date=run_date,
309	        horizon_days=horizon_days,
310	        warehouse_id=warehouse_id,
311	        demand_source="sales-order demand + reorder points",
312	    )
313	    session.add(run)
314	    await session.flush()
315	    await docflow.set_document_status(
316	        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=run_number, status=MrpRunStatus.RUNNING.value
317	    )
318	    return run
319	
320	
321	async def run_mrp(
322	    session: AsyncSession,
323	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
324	    run_date: date,
325	    *,
326	    horizon_days: int = MRP_DEFAULT_HORIZON_DAYS,
327	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
328	) -> MrpRun:
329	    """Execute one deterministic MRP run (module docstring): regenerate un-firmed planned orders,
330	    net demand against supply level by level (exploding MAKE items' BOMs), bulk-write the fresh
331	    planned orders, then run the rough capacity check — all in the caller's uow (the job's). Returns
332	    the COMPLETED run. Caller commits via uow (D-011)."""
333	    run = await _create_run(session, tenant_id, run_date, horizon_days, warehouse_id)
334	    await _regenerate(session, tenant_id)
335	    lines = await _plan_levels(session, tenant_id)
336	
337	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
338	    make_count = 0
339	    buy_count = 0
340	    for line in lines:
341	        if line.order_type == PlannedOrderType.MAKE.value:
342	            make_count += 1
343	        else:
344	            buy_count += 1
345	        rows.append(
346	            {
347	                "id": uuid.uuid4(),
348	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
349	                "mrp_run_id": run.id,
350	                "item_id": line.item_id,
351	                "order_type": line.order_type,
352	                "quantity": line.quantity,
353	                "due_date": run_date,
354	                "status": PlannedOrderStatus.PLANNED.value,
355	                "source_notes": line.source_notes,
356	                "level": line.level,
357	                "converted_document_id": None,
358	            }
359	        )
360	    if rows:
361	        await session.execute(insert(PlannedOrder), rows)
362	
363	    await rough_capacity_check(session, tenant_id, run.id, horizon_days)
364	
365	    run.status = MrpRunStatus.COMPLETED.value
366	    run.planned_make_count = make_count
367	    run.planned_buy_count = buy_count
368	    run.completed_at = datetime.now(UTC)
369	    await session.flush()
370	    await docflow.set_document_status(
371	        session, tenant_id, run.document_id, status=MrpRunStatus.COMPLETED.value
372	    )
373	    return run
374	
375	
376	@register_job(MRP_RUN_JOB)
377	async def mrp_run_job(
378	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: dict[str, Any]
379	) -> dict[str, Any]:
380	    """Background-job handler (PERFORMANCE §3, D-049): the MRP run ALWAYS executes as a job and the
381	    endpoint returns 202 {job_id}. Delegates to :func:`run_mrp`."""
382	    run = await run_mrp(
383	        session,
384	        tenant_id,
385	        date.fromisoformat(payload["run_date"]),
386	        horizon_days=int(payload.get("horizon_days", MRP_DEFAULT_HORIZON_DAYS)),
387	        warehouse_id=(
388	            uuid.UUID(payload["warehouse_id"]) if payload.get("warehouse_id") else None
389	        ),
390	    )
391	    await session.refresh(run)
392	    return {
393	        "run_id": str(run.id),
394	        "run_number": run.run_number,
395	        "planned_make_count": run.planned_make_count,
396	        "planned_buy_count": run.planned_buy_count,
397	    }

1	"""Production-order DRAFT lifecycle (PLAN 8.2, D-048): create+explode, release, cancel + reads.
2	
3	The issue-to-WIP + finish-to-stock POSTING flows live in ``production_post.py`` (split at the
4	400-line cap, the sales delivery_post precedent); this file owns the DRAFT side. ``__init__``
5	re-exports both halves as one ``service`` surface.
6	
7	Rules enforced here (the service owns them, CLAUDE.md rule 7):
8	
9	- **create_production_order** — resolves the item's ACTIVE default BOM (or the supplied bom_id),
10	  EXPLODES its components into ``ProductionOrderComponent`` rows
11	  (required = quantity_per × order_qty × (1 + scrap_percent/100), quantized to the quantity scale),
12	  snapshots the active routing's operations into ``ProductionOrderOperation`` rows
13	  (planned_minutes = setup + run × order_qty), claims the gapless MO- number + registers the
14	  document, and validates the item is STOCKED, quantity > 0, the warehouse exists. SINGLE-LEVEL
15	  explosion: a sub-assembly component is itself produced by its OWN order (multi-level via
16	  references, D-047) — this order issues the sub-assembly as a finished material, it does not
17	  recurse.
18	- **release_order** — DRAFT→RELEASED; the component rows ARE the reservation (v1 ATP-style: release
19	  does NOT block on availability — a shortage is informational, the parity-doc backorder posture).
20	- **cancel_order** — DRAFT/RELEASED only; once a component is issued the order is POSTED-ish and
21	  must be FINISHED (issued stock + WIP cannot strand), so an IN_PROGRESS/FINISHED order is not
22	  cancellable.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import uuid
28	from datetime import date, datetime
29	from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
30	
31	from sqlalchemy import select

176	    bin; 422 when the warehouse has none (a component has nowhere to issue from)."""

189	async def create_production_order(
190	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ProductionOrderCreate
191	) -> ProductionOrder:
192	    """Create a DRAFT production order + EXPLODE its BOM into reserved component rows + SNAPSHOT
193	    its routing (D-048). Validates the parent item is STOCKED, quantity > 0 and the warehouse
194	    exists; resolves the BOM (active default unless supplied) and explodes required quantities
195	    (scrap-loaded, quantized); snapshots the routing operations' per-order load; registers the
196	    document + claims the MO- number. Born DRAFT — release reserves, issue consumes, finish
197	    produces."""
198	    quantity = Decimal(payload.quantity)
199	    if quantity <= 0:
200	        raise ValidationFailedError(
201	            message="Production quantity must be greater than zero",
202	            code="manufacturing.quantity_invalid",

205	    await _require_stocked_item(session, tenant_id, payload.item_id)
206	    bom = await _resolve_bom(session, tenant_id, payload)
207	    routing = await _resolve_routing(session, tenant_id, payload)

209	    components = await mfg_queries.bom_components(session, tenant_id, bom.id)

213	            code="manufacturing.bom_no_components",

217	    order_id = uuid.uuid4()
218	    document = await docflow.register_document(

235	        session, tenant_id, PRODUCTION_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=date.today()
236	    )

244	        item_id=payload.item_id,

247	        routing_id=routing.id if routing is not None else None,
248	        warehouse_id=payload.warehouse_id,
249	        planned_start_date=payload.planned_start_date,

251	        finished_quantity=Decimal(0),

253	        notes=payload.notes,
254	    )
255	    session.add(order)
256	    # The explosion factor scales component quantity_per (per the BOM's base_quantity) up to the
257	    # order quantity, then scrap loads each line. SINGLE-LEVEL: each direct component becomes one
258	    # reservation row — a sub-assembly is produced by its own order, this order consumes it as-is.
259	    base_quantity = Decimal(bom.base_quantity)
260	    for index, component in enumerate(components, start=1):

262	        required = _quantize_qty(

276	        )

278	    if routing is not None:
279	        operations = await mfg_queries.routing_operations(session, tenant_id, routing.id)
280	        for operation in operations:

282	                Decimal(operation.setup_time_minutes)
283	                + Decimal(operation.run_time_minutes_per_unit) * quantity
284	            )
285	            session.add(

293	                    run_time_minutes_per_unit=Decimal(operation.run_time_minutes_per_unit),
294	                    planned_minutes=planned,

309	async def release_order(
310	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
311	) -> ProductionOrder:
312	    """Release a DRAFT production order (D-048): DRAFT→RELEASED, materials reserved (the component
313	    rows ARE the reservation). Idempotent on an already-RELEASED order. The reservation does NOT
314	    block on availability — a shortage is informational (v1 ATP-style, the parity-doc backorder
315	    posture); a later phase can flag shortages without changing this transition. An IN_PROGRESS /
316	    FINISHED / CANCELLED order cannot be released."""
317	    order = await get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
318	    status = ProductionOrderStatus(order.status)
319	    if status == ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED:
320	        return order
321	    if status != ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT:
322	        raise ConflictError(
323	            message=f"A {order.status} production order cannot be released",
324	            code="manufacturing.production_order_not_releasable",
325	            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
326	        )
327	    order.status = ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value
328	    order.released_at = datetime.now()
329	    await session.flush()
330	    await docflow.set_document_status(
331	        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value
332	    )
333	    return order
334	
335	
336	async def cancel_order(
337	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
338	) -> ProductionOrder:
339	    """Cancel a DRAFT or RELEASED production order (D-048). Once a component has been issued the
340	    order is IN_PROGRESS — POSTED-ish: it has consumed stock to WIP, so it must be FINISHED (issued
341	    stock + WIP cannot strand; v1 has no reverse-issue), never cancelled. A FINISHED/CANCELLED order
342	    is terminal. Cancelling releases nothing physical (no component was issued)."""
343	    order = await get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
344	    status = ProductionOrderStatus(order.status)
345	    if status not in (ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT, ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED):
346	        raise ConflictError(
347	            message=f"A {order.status} production order cannot be cancelled",
348	            code="manufacturing.production_order_not_cancellable",
349	            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
350	        )
351	    order.status = ProductionOrderStatus.CANCELLED.value
352	    await session.flush()
353	    await docflow.set_document_status(
354	        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=ProductionOrderStatus.CANCELLED.value
355	    )
356	    return order

359	async def list_production_orders(
360	    session: AsyncSession,
361	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
362	    *,
363	    item_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
364	    status: ProductionOrderStatus | None = None,
365	    cursor: str | None = None,
366	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
367	) -> Page[ProductionOrder]:
368	    """Keyset-paginated production orders ordered by order_number (D-014). The item/status filters
369	    narrow the set (index-served by (tenant, status) / (tenant, item_id)) and fold into the cursor
370	    fingerprint."""
371	    stmt = select(ProductionOrder).where(ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id)
372	    if item_id is not None:
373	        stmt = stmt.where(ProductionOrder.item_id == item_id)
374	    if status is not None:
375	        stmt = stmt.where(ProductionOrder.status == status.value)

378	        session,

381	        pk=ProductionOrder.id,
382	        cursor=cursor,
383	        limit=limit,
384	        filters=fingerprint,
385	    )
