1	"""D-015 exact money/quantity/rate representation on BOTH engines, plus allocation.
2	
3	The financial engine's DB-level invariants (the balance trigger, the one-side CHECK,
4	valuation math) are only meaningful if storage is EXACT on both backends. PostgreSQL has a
5	native NUMERIC; SQLite does not — ``sa.Numeric`` round-trips through float there and silently
6	loses precision. So each TypeDecorator stores NUMERIC on Postgres and an INTEGER of scaled
7	minor units on SQLite (value × 10^scale), converting to/from ``decimal.Decimal`` in the bind/
8	result processors. Trigger SQL therefore only ever SUMs and COMPARES the stored representation
9	(ints on SQLite, NUMERIC on PG) — never divides or scales — so the asymmetric storage stays
10	semantically identical where it matters (D-015 trigger discipline).
11	
12	Scales:
13	- ``MoneyType``      NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — headroom over the
14	  2/3 currency decimals so posting-time rounding has somewhere to live.
15	- ``QuantityType``   NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — UoM/FIFO math.
16	- ``RateType``       NUMERIC(20,10) / INTEGER nano-units (×10^10), scale 10 — FX rates keep
17	  full precision (rates are never quantized to currency decimals).
18	
19	Python is Decimal-only — never float. The TypeDecorators are ``cache_ok = True`` (they carry
20	no per-instance state beyond the fixed class scale), so SQLAlchemy may cache compiled
21	statements that use them.
22	
23	``allocate`` is the single largest-remainder splitter (D-015): tax/discount splits, payment
24	allocation, and the journal's functional-currency residual-cent balancing all route through it
25	so parts always sum EXACTLY to the total. ``quantize_money`` is the ROUND_HALF_UP boundary
26	rounding (commercial/SAP practice), keyed off a per-currency decimal-places lookup.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
32	
33	import sqlalchemy as sa
34	from sqlalchemy.engine import Dialect
35	from sqlalchemy.types import TypeDecorator
36	
37	# Scales (number of fractional decimal digits each type stores).
38	_MONEY_SCALE = 6
39	_QUANTITY_SCALE = 6
40	_RATE_SCALE = 10
41	
42	
43	class _ScaledDecimalType(TypeDecorator[Decimal]):
44	    """Shared base for the three exact-decimal types (D-015).
45	
46	    ``impl`` is NUMERIC so the default (Postgres) rendering is a true decimal; on SQLite the
47	    column is loaded as INTEGER and the bind/result processors translate Decimal <-> scaled
48	    integer minor units. The conversion is exact in both directions because a Decimal with at
49	    most ``scale`` fractional digits maps to an integer with no rounding (values carrying more
50	    digits than the scale are quantized HALF_UP on the way in — money/quantities are quantized
51	    at their boundary before storage, so this only ever trims trailing noise)."""
52	
53	    # Required by TypeDecorator: the default (Postgres) decorated type. ``load_dialect_impl``
54	    # overrides it per dialect (BigInteger on SQLite, Numeric(precision, scale) on PG).
55	    impl = sa.Numeric
56	    cache_ok = True
57	
58	    # Concrete subclasses set these; the base is abstract by virtue of unset class attrs.
59	    scale: int
60	    precision: int
61	
62	    @property
63	    def python_type(self) -> type[Decimal]:
64	        return Decimal
65	
66	    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect: Dialect) -> sa.types.TypeEngine[object]:
67	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
68	            # Scaled minor units fit a 64-bit integer for the demo/test value ranges (D-015).
69	            return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.BigInteger())
70	        return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.Numeric(self.precision, self.scale))
71	
72	    @property
73	    def _quantum(self) -> Decimal:
74	        return Decimal(1).scaleb(-self.scale)
75	
76	    def process_bind_param(self, value: Decimal | int | str | None, dialect: Dialect):
77	        if value is None:
78	            return None
79	        as_decimal = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
80	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
81	            # Decimal -> integer scaled minor units. Quantize first so a value with more than
82	            # ``scale`` digits cannot leave a fractional remainder when multiplied out.
83	            scaled = as_decimal.quantize(self._quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
84	            return int(scaled.scaleb(self.scale))
85	        return as_decimal
86	
87	    def process_result_value(self, value: int | Decimal | None, dialect: Dialect) -> Decimal | None:
88	        if value is None:
89	            return None
90	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
91	            # Integer scaled minor units -> Decimal at the type's scale (exact, no float).
92	            return (Decimal(int(value)) * self._quantum).quantize(self._quantum)
93	        return value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
94	
95	
96	class MoneyType(_ScaledDecimalType):
97	    """Monetary amount (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite."""
98	
99	    # cache_ok must be set on each concrete TypeDecorator class, not just the base.
100	    cache_ok = True
101	    scale = _MONEY_SCALE
102	    precision = 18
103	
104	
105	class QuantityType(_ScaledDecimalType):
106	    """Inventory quantity (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite.
107	    Same storage as MoneyType but a distinct type so quantity and money columns read clearly."""
108	
109	    cache_ok = True
110	    scale = _QUANTITY_SCALE
111	    precision = 18
112	
113	
114	class RateType(_ScaledDecimalType):
115	    """FX/exchange rate (D-015): NUMERIC(20,10) on Postgres, INTEGER nano-units on SQLite.
116	    Scale 10 keeps full rate precision — rates are never quantized to currency decimals."""
117	
118	    cache_ok = True
119	    scale = _RATE_SCALE
120	    precision = 20
121	
122	
123	# --- Currency decimals + boundary rounding ------------------------------------
124	
125	# ISO 4217 fractional digits. Default is 2; non-2-decimal currencies are listed explicitly so
126	# the table can grow (JPY=0, BHD=3, ...). Stored journal amounts quantize to this at the
127	# posting/pricing boundary; unit prices/costs and FX rates keep full scale-6/10 precision.
128	_DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS = 2
129	_CURRENCY_DECIMALS: dict[str, int] = {
130	    "JPY": 0,
131	    "KRW": 0,
132	    "BHD": 3,
133	    "KWD": 3,
134	    "OMR": 3,
135	    "TND": 3,
136	}
137	
138	
139	def currency_decimals(currency_code: str) -> int:
140	    """ISO 4217 fractional digits for ``currency_code`` (default 2). The amount-rounding
141	    boundary uses this so e.g. JPY rounds to whole units and BHD to three places (D-015)."""
142	    return _CURRENCY_DECIMALS.get(currency_code.upper(), _DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS)
143	
144	
145	def quantize_money(value: Decimal, places: int = 2) -> Decimal:
146	    """Round ``value`` to ``places`` decimals HALF_UP (D-015 — commercial/SAP practice). Pass
147	    ``currency_decimals(code)`` for ``places`` to round to a currency's minor unit."""
148	    return value.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
149	
150	
151	def quantize_for_currency(value: Decimal, currency_code: str) -> Decimal:
152	    """Round ``value`` to ``currency_code``'s minor unit HALF_UP (D-015)."""
153	    return quantize_money(value, currency_decimals(currency_code))
154	
155	
156	def allocate(total: Decimal, weights: list[Decimal], places: int = 2) -> list[Decimal]:
157	    """Split ``total`` across ``weights`` so the parts sum EXACTLY to ``total`` (D-015).
158	
159	    Largest-remainder method: each part is ``total × weight / Σweights`` rounded DOWN to
160	    ``places`` decimals, then the rounding residual (``total`` minus the sum of floored parts)
161	    is distributed one minor unit at a time to the parts with the largest fractional remainder,
162	    ties broken by original index. Deterministic, and the parts ALWAYS reconstitute the total —
163	    used for FX residual-cent absorption, tax splits, discount splits and payment allocation.
164	
165	    A zero or empty total returns zeros; zero total weight (all weights zero) splits ``total``
166	    evenly via equal unit weights so the result still sums to ``total`` rather than dropping it.
167	    """
168	    quantum = Decimal(1).scaleb(-places)
169	    n = len(weights)
170	    if n == 0:
171	        return []
172	    total_weight = sum(weights, Decimal(0))
173	    if total_weight == 0:
174	        # Degenerate: no weight to distribute by. Fall back to equal weights so the total is
175	        # still allocated exactly (never silently dropped).
176	        weights = [Decimal(1)] * n
177	        total_weight = Decimal(n)
178	
179	    exact = [total * weight / total_weight for weight in weights]
180	    floored = [part.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_DOWN) for part in exact]
181	    remainders = [exact[i] - floored[i] for i in range(n)]
182	
183	    allocated = sum(floored, Decimal(0))
184	    residual = total - allocated
185	    # Number of whole minor units still to hand out (can be negative if total is negative).
186	    units = int((residual / quantum).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
187	
188	    # Distribute to the largest remainders first; for a negative residual hand out negative
189	    # units to the SMALLEST remainders (those rounded least-down) so the result stays balanced.
190	    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (remainders[i], -i), reverse=units >= 0)
191	    step = quantum if units >= 0 else -quantum
192	    for k in range(abs(units)):
193	        floored[order[k % n]] += step
194	    return floored
195	
196	
197	__all__ = [
198	    "MoneyType",
199	    "QuantityType",
200	    "RateType",
201	    "allocate",
202	    "currency_decimals",
203	    "quantize_for_currency",
204	    "quantize_money",
205	]

1	"""Production-order HTTP layer (PLAN 8.2), included into the manufacturing router.
2	
3	A sibling sub-router under the same ``/api/v1/manufacturing`` prefix, mounted by
4	``router.include_router`` in router.py (the bom_router/routing_router precedent — ONE module
5	surface,
6	no second mount in main.py).
7	
8	RBAC (D-009; distinct authorities):
9	  - read by ``manufacturing.production_order.read``;
10	  - create+explode / cancel the order by ``manufacturing.production_order.manage``;
11	  - release (reserve materials) by ``manufacturing.production_order.release``;
12	- issue components + finish to stock by ``manufacturing.production_order.execute`` (both POST stock
13	    + WIP journals — the shop-floor action).
14	
15	Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so the order + its N stock ISSUE/RECEIPT moves + N WIP
16	journals + the order update commit (or roll back) atomically; the document-creating + issue + finish
17	endpoints are IDEMPOTENT (D-013). The list is O(1) queries + paginated (PERFORMANCE §6).
18	"""

85	    and none is supplied. IDEMPOTENT (D-013)."""

137	    order_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
138	) -> ProductionOrderDetail:
139	    """Release a DRAFT order — reserve materials (DRAFT→RELEASED, PLAN 8.2)."""

142	    async def work() -> None:

1	"""Conditional GETs on slow-changing reference data — collection-level weak ETags (D-035).
2	
3	PERFORMANCE §3 requires ``ETag/If-None-Match`` on slow-changing reference collections (chart of
4	accounts, currencies, tax codes, fiscal calendar, posting defaults). This is a justified core
5	flat file (the same precedent as core/pagination.py): the validator machinery is cross-cutting,
6	mentions no business concept, and every reference endpoint composes it the same way.
7	
8	**Why collection-level, not row-level.** A row-level ETag would validate one entity; a list
9	endpoint returns a *page* of a collection, and the cheapest correct validator for "has anything in
10	this collection changed?" is a single aggregate ``SELECT COUNT(id), MAX(updated_at)`` over the
11	tenant's rows. Any insert moves the count; any update moves ``MAX(updated_at)`` (TimestampMixin's
12	``onupdate``); a delete moves the count (and usually the max). So the pair ``(count, max_updated)``
13	is a sound WEAK validator for the whole collection. The cost: any change to the collection
14	invalidates *every* page's cached validator — acceptable for small reference sets, which is exactly
15	the data this is applied to (PERFORMANCE §3 scopes it to reference data only, never transactional
16	lists). Deletes that leave count unchanged are impossible for a pure delete; a delete-then-insert
17	in the same instant could in principle pin both count and max, so we additionally guard correctness
18	with the request fingerprint below — but for the data this covers the (count, max) pair is the
19	dominant signal.
20	
21	**Tenant component (D-007).** The aggregate select references the model's columns
22	(``func.count(model.id)``), so the ``do_orm_execute`` tenancy listener engages and scopes the
23	COUNT/MAX to the current tenant automatically (verified: a ``func`` aggregate over mapped columns
24	carries the mapper, so ``all_mappers`` detects it). The tenant id is *also* baked into the ETag
25	string as a short component, so even if two tenants happened to hold the same (count, max) the
26	validators differ — a cross-tenant 304 is impossible by construction, belt-and-suspenders over the
27	already tenant-scoped aggregate.
28	
29	**Request fingerprint (the key correctness point).** The ETag represents the *whole collection's*
30	version, not one page. A naive collection-level validator would let a client that cached page 2
31	receive a 304 for a request for page 5 (same collection, unchanged) and then render the wrong
32	slice. To prevent that, the request's cursor + limit + filters are hashed into the ETag, so the
33	validator is unique per (collection-version, page-request). A 304 can therefore only ever be served
34	for the *identical* page request whose body the client already holds.
35	
36	**Format.** ``W/"<count>-<max_updated_at_micros>-<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"`` — a weak validator
37	(``W/`` prefix) because two byte-different but semantically-equal page renderings (e.g. ordering
38	ties) should still match. Empty collection → ``W/"0--<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"`` (a stable
39	``max`` component of empty string), which still changes the moment the first row is inserted.
40	"""
41	
42	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
43	
44	import sqlalchemy as sa
45	from fastapi import Request, Response
46	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
47	
48	from app.core.tenancy import get_current_tenant_id
49	
50	# 304 carries no body; only the validator header rides back so the client can revalidate again.
51	NOT_MODIFIED_STATUS = 304
52	
53	
54	def _tenant_component() -> str:
55	    """Short, stable tenant marker for the ETag. The aggregate is already tenant-scoped by the
56	    D-007 listener; this makes a cross-tenant validator collision impossible even in theory, since
57	    two tenants' validators differ in this component regardless of their (count, max). Reads the
58	    request's tenant from the ContextVar (set by core/deps.get_current_user)."""
59	    tenant_id = get_current_tenant_id()
60	    # get_current_tenant_id is fail-closed and only returns None under system_context, which a
61	    # tenant reference endpoint never runs under; guard anyway so the helper is total.
62	    return tenant_id.hex[:8] if tenant_id is not None else "system"
63	
64	
65	async def collection_etag(
66	    session: AsyncSession,
67	    model: type,
68	    *extra_filters: sa.ColumnElement[bool],
69	    request_fingerprint: str = "",
70	) -> str:
71	    """Compute a WEAK collection validator from ONE cheap aggregate query (D-035).
72	
73	    ``SELECT COUNT(model.id), MAX(model.updated_at)`` — tenant-scoped automatically by the D-007
74	    ``do_orm_execute`` listener (the aggregate references the model's mapped columns, so the
75	    tenant predicate is injected). ``extra_filters`` narrow the collection to the same rows the
76	    list endpoint returns (e.g. a ``fiscal_year_id`` filter), so the validator tracks the visible
77	    slice, not the whole table. ``request_fingerprint`` (cursor+limit+filters of the actual
78	    request) is folded into the returned tag so a 304 can never serve a different page slice.
79	
80	    The returned string is the full weak ETag ready for the ``ETag`` header / ``If-None-Match``
81	    comparison: ``W/"<count>-<max_micros>-<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"``.
82	    """
83	    stmt = sa.select(sa.func.count(model.id), sa.func.max(model.updated_at))
84	    for clause in extra_filters:
85	        stmt = stmt.where(clause)
86	    count, max_updated = (await session.execute(stmt)).one()
87	
88	    # Microsecond epoch keeps the component compact and monotonic; empty collection → "" so the
89	    # validator is stable for an empty set yet flips the moment the first row lands (count 0->1).
90	    max_component = (
91	        "" if max_updated is None else str(int(max_updated.timestamp() * 1_000_000))
92	    )
93	    return f'W/"{count}-{max_component}-{_tenant_component()}-{request_fingerprint}"'
94	
95	
96	def _normalize_tag(raw: str) -> str:
97	    """Strip a leading weak marker so weak/strong forms of the same tag compare equal. Per RFC
98	    7232 the weak-comparison function ignores the ``W/`` prefix; our validators are always weak,
99	    but a client may echo the value with or without it, so normalize both sides."""
100	    raw = raw.strip()
101	    if raw.startswith("W/"):
102	        raw = raw[2:]
103	    return raw
104	
105	
106	def check_not_modified(request: Request, etag: str) -> bool:
107	    """True when the client's ``If-None-Match`` satisfies ``etag`` (RFC 7232 weak comparison).
108	
109	    Handles the ``*`` value (matches any existing representation → 304 whenever the resource
110	    exists) and a comma-separated list of candidate tags. Comparison is weak: the ``W/`` prefix is
111	    ignored on both sides. A missing/blank header → False (the endpoint then serves a normal 200).
112	    """
113	    header = request.headers.get("if-none-match")
114	    if not header:
115	        return False
116	    candidates = [part.strip() for part in header.split(",") if part.strip()]
117	    if "*" in candidates:
118	        return True
119	    target = _normalize_tag(etag)
120	    return any(_normalize_tag(candidate) == target for candidate in candidates)
121	
122	
123	async def conditional_response[T](
124	    request: Request,
125	    response: Response,
126	    etag: str,
127	    builder: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]],
128	) -> T | Response:
129	    """Conditional-GET epilogue for a reference list endpoint (D-035).
130	
131	    Given the already-computed collection ``etag``: if the client's ``If-None-Match`` matches,
132	    return a bare ``304`` carrying ONLY the ``ETag`` header and NO body — and crucially WITHOUT
133	    awaiting ``builder``, so the expensive full-page query never runs on the 304 path (this is what
134	    makes a conditional request cheaper than the unconditional one). Otherwise set the ``ETag``
135	    header on the real response and return ``await builder()`` (the ``Page`` payload).
136	
137	    Returning a starlette ``Response`` directly bypasses the route's ``response_model``, so FastAPI
138	    does not try to validate the empty 304 body against ``Page[T]`` (verified by a test).
139	    """
140	    if check_not_modified(request, etag):
141	        return Response(status_code=NOT_MODIFIED_STATUS, headers={"ETag": etag})
142	    response.headers["ETag"] = etag
143	    return await builder()
144	
145	
146	def request_fingerprint(cursor: str | None, limit: int, *filter_parts: object) -> str:
147	    """Stable per-request fingerprint folded into the collection ETag so a 304 can only ever be
148	    served for the IDENTICAL page request (D-035). Reuses the pagination filter-fingerprint hash so
149	    the cursor/limit/filter identity matches what ``paginate`` already keys cursors on — one source
150	    of truth for "which slice of the collection is this request asking for"."""
151	    # Imported lazily: core/pagination imports core/schemas which is heavy; keeping the import here
152	    # avoids any import-order coupling and this helper is called per request, not at module load.
153	    from app.core.pagination import filter_fingerprint
154	
155	    return filter_fingerprint(cursor, limit, *filter_parts)
156	
157	
158	__all__ = [
159	    "check_not_modified",
160	    "collection_etag",
161	    "conditional_response",
162	    "request_fingerprint",
163	]

37	@dataclass(frozen=True)
38	class InspectionLotSetup:
39	    """A tenant with a posted, inspection-FLAGGED goods receipt that auto-created an OPEN inspection
40	    lot (PLAN 9.1). Plain ids so a rollback (expiring loaded ORM objects) cannot break a follow-up
41	    payload. ``lot_id`` is the created inspection lot; ``bin_id`` is the receiving bin the stock
42	    landed in (a SCRAP/BLOCK moves from it); ``blocked_bin_id`` is a second bin in the same
43	    warehouse
44	    used as the BLOCK quarantine destination; ``gr_document_id`` is the GR's core_documents id (the
45	    lot's source + the docflow predecessor)."""
46	
47	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
48	    item_id: uuid.UUID
49	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
50	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
51	    blocked_bin_id: uuid.UUID
52	    gr_id: uuid.UUID
53	    gr_document_id: uuid.UUID
54	    lot_id: uuid.UUID
55	    lot_quantity: Decimal
56	    price_difference_account_id: uuid.UUID
57	    inventory_account_id: uuid.UUID
58	    fiscal_year_id: uuid.UUID

61	async def build_inspection_lot_setup(
62	    session: AsyncSession,
63	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
64	    *,
65	    receive_quantity: str = "10",
66	    po_unit_cost: str = "5",
67	) -> InspectionLotSetup:
68	    """Wire a flagged, posted goods receipt so an OPEN inspection lot exists (PLAN 9.1). Builds the
69	    goods-receipt setup, creates a GR with one line flagged ``requires_inspection=True``, posts it
70	    (the quality handler creates the lot), and returns the created lot + a second quarantine bin."""
71	    from tests.modules.inventory.factories import build_bin
72	
73	    gr_setup = await build_goods_receipt_setup(
74	        session, tenant_id, po_quantity=receive_quantity, po_unit_cost=po_unit_cost
75	    )
76	    blocked_bin = await build_bin(
77	        session, tenant_id, gr_setup.warehouse_id, code="QI", name="Quality hold"
78	    )
79	    gr = await build_goods_receipt(
80	        session,
81	        tenant_id,
82	        po_id=gr_setup.po_id,
83	        warehouse_id=gr_setup.warehouse_id,
84	        lines=[
85	            GoodsReceiptLineCreate(
86	                purchase_order_line_id=gr_setup.po_line_id,
87	                bin_id=gr_setup.bin_id,
88	                received_quantity=Decimal(receive_quantity),
89	                requires_inspection=True,
90	            )
91	        ],
92	    )
93	    await post_goods_receipt(session, tenant_id, gr.id)
94	    with tenant_context(tenant_id):
95	        gr_reloaded = await procurement_service.get_goods_receipt(session, tenant_id, gr.id)
96	        gr_document_id = gr_reloaded.document_id
97	        lots = await quality_queries.lots_for_goods_receipt(
98	            session, tenant_id, gr_document_id
99	        )
100	    return InspectionLotSetup(
101	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
102	        item_id=gr_setup.item_id,
103	        warehouse_id=gr_setup.warehouse_id,
104	        bin_id=gr_setup.bin_id,
105	        blocked_bin_id=blocked_bin.id,
106	        gr_id=gr.id,
107	        gr_document_id=gr_document_id,
108	        lot_id=lots[0].id,
109	        lot_quantity=Decimal(receive_quantity),
110	        price_difference_account_id=gr_setup.price_difference_account_id,
111	        inventory_account_id=gr_setup.inventory_account_id,
112	        fiscal_year_id=gr_setup.fiscal_year_id,
113	    )
114	
115	
116	# --- Principals ---------------------------------------------------------------
117	
118	# EVERY registered quality.* key (importing quality.constants registers them), so a new quality
119	# permission is auto-granted to the full-rights principal (self-extending). The flagged goods
120	# receipt
121	# the lot derives from is seeded through the db_session factories (system context), not over the
122	# wire,
123	# so the principal needs only the quality keys to drive the inspection-lot endpoints — the
124	# production_api precedent (setup seeded via factories, client drives only the module's own routes).
125	_QUALITY_KEYS = tuple(sorted(key for key in catalog_keys() if key.startswith("quality.")))
126	
127	
128	@dataclass(frozen=True)
129	class QualityPrincipal:
130	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
131	    tenant_slug: str
132	    user_id: uuid.UUID
133	    email: str
134	    password: str
135	
136	
137	async def create_quality_principal(
138	    session: AsyncSession,
139	    slug: str = "qm-acme",
140	    email: str = "qa@qm-acme.test",
141	    password: str = "correct-horse-battery",
142	    keys: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
143	) -> QualityPrincipal:
144	    """Provision a tenant + user and grant a role with the quality permission keys through the real
145	    services (D-025); ``keys`` narrows the grant for the 403 RBAC tests (None = full)."""
146	    grant = keys if keys is not None else _QUALITY_KEYS
147	    tenant = await provision_tenant(session, slug=slug, name=slug.title())
148	    user = await provision_user(session, tenant.id, email=email, password=password)
149	    with system_context():
150	        await sync_permission_catalog(session)
151	    role = await create_role(session, tenant.id, "Quality", grant, is_system=True)
152	    await assign_role(session, tenant.id, user.id, role.id, user.token_version)
153	    await session.commit()
154	    return QualityPrincipal(
155	        tenant_id=tenant.id,
156	        tenant_slug=slug,
157	        user_id=user.id,
158	        email=email,
159	        password=password,
160	    )

9	posted flagged GR creates a lot and a reject decision moves stock + posts the write-off exactly as

DECISIONS.md:36:- **D-032 Background-job core (PLAN 4P.5, closes #26): code-defined registry + in-process asyncio runner behind a scheduler seam; `core_jobs` not audited:** `core/jobs.py` owns the `Job` model (`core_jobs`: job_type/status/payload/result/error/submitted_by/started+finished, indexes `(tenant_id, status)` + `(tenant_id, job_type, created_at)`; migration 0017), a `@register_job` registry (code-defined like permissions), `submit_job` (PENDING row flushed inside the endpoint's uow so it commits atomically with the D-013 idempotency capture — a replayed key returns the SAME job id), and the runner: scheduled via `schedule_job(job_id, session_factory)` strictly AFTER the uow commit (no visibility race), it opens its own session from the factory the router's `get_session_factory` dependency supplied (production = app factory; tests = the per-test-engine override, which is how the runner lands in the right DB in both worlds), restores `tenant_context(tenant_id)` + the D-010 actor ContextVar from `submitted_by_user_id`, marks RUNNING (own commit), runs the handler inside `run_in_uow` with COMPLETED+result set in the same uow (business writes and terminal status are atomic; events + audit behave exactly as in-request), and on any exception commits only FAILED + the truncated error. Concurrency capped at 4 via per-event-loop semaphores (asyncio primitives bind to their first loop; tests run one loop per test); `wait_for_jobs()` makes tests deterministic. SWAP SEAM: submitters call `schedule_job`, delegating to the module `scheduler: JobScheduler` Protocol singleton (the D-011 bus pattern) — a queue runner (arq/celery) rebinds it, ignoring the session-factory argument, with zero submitter changes. Polling: `core/jobs_router.py` (`GET /api/v1/jobs[/{id}]`, auth-only + tenant-scoped, paginated — the D-027 core-router precedent). `core_jobs` is deliberately NOT audited: high-churn control rows (PENDING→RUNNING→terminal per job), same documented exclusion class as `core_refresh_sessions`/`core_idempotency_keys`; the handler's BUSINESS writes are audited normally with the submitting user as actor. The #26 fix: `POST /finance/fx-revaluation-runs` and `POST /finance/payment-runs` now submit `finance.fx_revaluation`/`finance.payment_run` jobs and return `202 {job_id, status}` (service functions unchanged; the retired sync `PaymentRunResult` wrapper was deleted — payment ids/numbers ride the job result). Model registration deviation: `core/jobs` imports `core/audit` (actor ContextVar), so like idempotency it registers on `Base.metadata` from the BOTTOM of `core/db.py`, not models.py's trailing imports (a trailing import dead-locks on the audit->models cycle).

86	@dataclass
87	class QueryCounter:
88	    """Counts real SQL statements executed on the per-test engine while active.
89	
90	    Used as a context manager: ``with query_counter() as qc: ...`` then read ``qc.count``.
91	    The ``after_cursor_execute`` listener attaches to the TEST engine's sync engine on enter
92	    and detaches on exit (per-use, so the per-test engine pattern stays leak-free).
93	    Transaction-control statements (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/RELEASE) and PRAGMAs are
94	    excluded — the budget measures real SELECT/INSERT/... statements. ``statements`` keeps
95	    the counted SQL so a budget failure shows exactly which queries ran.
96	    """
97	
98	    sync_engine: Engine
99	    count: int = 0
100	    statements: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
101	
102	    _IGNORED_PREFIXES = ("BEGIN", "COMMIT", "ROLLBACK", "SAVEPOINT", "RELEASE", "PRAGMA")
103	
104	    def _after_cursor_execute(
105	        self,
106	        conn: Any,
107	        cursor: Any,
108	        statement: str,
109	        parameters: Any,
110	        context: Any,
111	        executemany: bool,
112	    ) -> None:
113	        if statement.lstrip().upper().startswith(self._IGNORED_PREFIXES):
114	            return
115	        self.count += 1
116	        self.statements.append(statement)
117	
118	    def __enter__(self) -> "QueryCounter":
119	        self.count = 0
120	        self.statements = []
121	        event.listen(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)
122	        return self
123	
124	    def __exit__(
125	        self,
126	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
127	        exc: BaseException | None,
128	        tb: TracebackType | None,
129	    ) -> None:
130	        event.remove(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)

130:# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)
===TAIL===
| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |

Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.

# 8. File-Handling Rules

1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.
5. **One concept per file.** A file named `journal.py` containing tax logic is misfiled even if it compiles. Filename promises content.
6. **Generated files are never hand-edited** (OpenAPI dumps, lockfiles, migration auto-generations get reviewed and adjusted only through their tooling). Commit lockfiles; never commit build output, caches, coverage reports, or `__pycache__` — keep `.gitignore` authoritative.
7. **No utils graveyards.** Before adding to a `utils`-like file, ask which module/concern owns the function; `core/` files and `lib/format.ts` are the only sanctioned shared helpers, each scoped by its filename.
8. **Imports:** absolute imports only in backend (`from app.modules.finance.service import journal`); frontend uses the `@/` alias (`@/lib/apiClient`). No relative `../../..` chains.
9. **Module READMEs are forbidden** — module docs live in `docs/modules/<module>.md` only, so documentation has one home.
10. **Renames/moves** are their own commit (`refactor(structure): move costing into inventory/service/costing.py`), never mixed with logic changes, so history stays traceable.
11. **Deletions** follow issue-first if the file contains live logic being retired: file the issue, explain replacement, delete in the fix PR.
12. **After compaction:** before creating ANY new file, re-read this document and run `git status` + `tree -L 3` (or `find`) to re-anchor on the actual current structure. Never recreate from memory a file that might already exist.

# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)

Any file outside the canonical tree? Any file over the size cap? Any duplicate concept names (`grep` a few suspects)? Any orphan files? Any module breaking the dependency rules? Any term drift (supplier vs vendor)? Each "yes" becomes a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6, fixed before the next promotion.

"""Maintenance module (PLAN 9.2) — the SEVENTH business module (s4hana-parity QM/PM).

PLAN 9.2 OPENS the Plant-Maintenance side of the parity QM/PM area with the DELIBERATELY SMALL PM
core the parity doc scopes (docs/research/s4hana-parity.md §QM/PM): an EQUIPMENT register, CORRECTIVE
maintenance orders (created ad-hoc against a piece of equipment), and PREVENTIVE maintenance via
interval-based PLANS that GENERATE due orders on a periodic run. Everything else PM (functional
location hierarchies, maintenance notifications, measurement points/counters, task lists, and
counter/strategy-based scheduling) is explicitly OUT of v1 — recorded in the parity doc (D-051).

Maintenance sits ABOVE finance in the dependency order (STRUCTURE §5 / D-051). It:

- READS via ``finance/queries.cost_center_exists`` DOWNWARD (D-029) — an equipment's optional cost
  centre for cost attribution — never finance models, never a cross-module FK.
- Does NOT subscribe to or publish any cross-module event in v1: a completed maintenance order
  RECORDS its ``actual_cost`` on the order row (record-only — no GL posting, D-051). The parity scope
  is "equipment register + corrective/preventive orders", not full work-order costing; a GL posting
  through the cost centre is a documented later. So there is NO events.py / handlers.py here (an empty
  event file would be a dead file — STRUCTURE §8.3).

No cycle (D-051): finance is an OLDER module and imports nothing from maintenance, so
maintenance→finance/queries is one-directional (STRUCTURE §5 bans only bidirectional query imports).
``maintenance/queries.py`` is the only file a later module would import.

The PREVENTIVE generation run scans the tenant's ACTIVE plans whose ``next_due_date`` has arrived and

maintenance-order document type / number sequence / docflow links, registered into the core RBAC
catalog at import (D-009).

A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap) — PLAN
9.2's small PM core sits well under that.

IDENTITY + NUMBERING (D-051). The two MASTERS carry no gapless document number: ``Equipment`` and
``MaintenancePlan`` use a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` unique per tenant (the work-centre / item-code
master precedent). A MAINTENANCE ORDER, by contrast, IS a posted document in the D-012 sense: it
registers in core_documents and claims a gapless number at creation.

PREFIX CHOICE (D-051). The order prefix is **"MNT-"** (maintenance), NOT "MO-": "MO-" is already the
manufacturing PRODUCTION-order prefix, and "WO-" (work order) was the alternative but "MNT-" reads
unambiguously as maintenance and never collides with PO-/GR-/SO-/DN-/MO-/MRP-/QL-.

SCOPE (s4hana-parity §QM/PM, D-051). v1 is equipment + corrective/preventive orders + interval plans.
No functional locations, no notifications, no measurement points/counters, no task lists. A
maintenance order tracks a free-text description + labour/cost as simple amounts; spare-part stock
issue and a PM→FI GL posting are documented laters (the cost is recorded on the order, record-only).
"""

from enum import StrEnum

from app.core.rbac import register_permissions


class EquipmentStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a piece of EQUIPMENT (PLAN 9.2, D-051). A flat equipment register — no functional
    location hierarchy (out of v1 scope).

    - **ACTIVE** — in service; corrective orders may be raised and preventive plans may generate
      orders against it. The default at creation.
    - **INACTIVE** — temporarily out of service (e.g. mothballed). Existing orders stay; a new
      CORRECTIVE order cannot be raised against it (v1 rule: a maintenance order targets ACTIVE
      equipment only).
    - **RETIRED** — permanently decommissioned. Terminal; like INACTIVE it blocks new orders.
    """

    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
    RETIRED = "RETIRED"


class MaintenanceOrderType(StrEnum):
    """How a MAINTENANCE ORDER originated (PLAN 9.2, D-051).

    - **CORRECTIVE** — a break-fix order created AD-HOC against a piece of equipment (a breakdown /
      repair). It has no plan link.
    - **PREVENTIVE** — a scheduled order GENERATED by an interval-based maintenance PLAN's run. It
      carries ``maintenance_plan_id`` and a plan→order docflow edge.
    """

    CORRECTIVE = "CORRECTIVE"
    PREVENTIVE = "PREVENTIVE"


class MaintenanceOrderStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a MAINTENANCE ORDER (PLAN 9.2, D-051). The service owns every transition
    (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

    - **DRAFT** — created (a corrective order with no schedule yet). Editable via schedule/cancel.
    - **SCHEDULED** — given a planned ``scheduled_date`` and ready to execute. A PREVENTIVE order is
      born SCHEDULED (the run sets its ``scheduled_date`` = the plan's due date); a CORRECTIVE order
      is created DRAFT or SCHEDULED.
    - **IN_PROGRESS** — work has started.
    - **COMPLETED** — work finished; ``actual_cost`` + ``completed_date`` are recorded. Terminal.
      v1 records the cost ON THE ORDER only (record-only — no GL posting, D-051).
    - **CANCELLED** — abandoned before completion (DRAFT/SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS). Terminal.
    """

    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    SCHEDULED = "SCHEDULED"
    IN_PROGRESS = "IN_PROGRESS"
    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"


class MaintenancePlanStatus(StrEnum):
    """Lifecycle of a MAINTENANCE PLAN (PLAN 9.2, D-051). A plan defines a recurring preventive task
    on a piece of equipment; the generation run creates orders from ACTIVE plans.

    - **ACTIVE** — the run considers it: when ``next_due_date <= as_of`` it generates a PREVENTIVE
      order and advances the plan. The default at creation.
    - **INACTIVE** — paused: the run skips it (no orders generated) until reactivated.
    """

    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"


class IntervalUnit(StrEnum):
    """The UNIT of a maintenance plan's preventive interval (PLAN 9.2, D-051). ``interval_value`` ×
    this unit is the recurrence (e.g. every 3 MONTHS). v1 is purely TIME-based — counter/performance
    intervals need measurement points, which are out of scope.

    - **DAYS** / **WEEKS** / **MONTHS** — the interval is advanced by N calendar days/weeks/months
      from the last generated due date (MONTHS uses calendar-month arithmetic, D-051).
    """

    DAYS = "DAYS"
    WEEKS = "WEEKS"
    MONTHS = "MONTHS"

# Equipment + plan masters split read/manage; the ORDER splits read/manage/complete because
# COMPLETE records the actual cost (a distinct, value-bearing action — the journal.post / quality

MAINTENANCE_PLAN_READ = "maintenance.plan.read"
MAINTENANCE_PLAN_MANAGE = "maintenance.plan.manage"
MAINTENANCE_PLAN_RUN = "maintenance.plan.run"

    MAINTENANCE_ORDER_MANAGE,

        MAINTENANCE_EQUIPMENT_MANAGE: "Create and edit equipment",
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_READ: "Read maintenance orders",
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_MANAGE: "Create, schedule, start and cancel maintenance orders",
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_COMPLETE: "Complete maintenance orders (record actual cost)",

"""Maintenance models (PLAN 9.2, parity PM = equipment register + corrective/preventive orders):
the ``Equipment`` register, the ``MaintenanceOrder`` document, and the interval-based
``MaintenancePlan``.

THREE tables, one concern (PM v1) — well under the 400-line cap, so a single models.py (the quality
precedent; split into a models/ package only at the cap).

- ``Equipment`` and ``MaintenancePlan`` are MASTERS keyed by a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` unique per
  tenant (no gapless number — the work-centre precedent). The plan ALSO mixes in DocumentMixin so it
  can be the docflow PREDECESSOR of the orders its run generates (the only master here that is a
  docflow source).
- ``MaintenanceOrder`` is a posted DOCUMENT (DocumentMixin + a gapless MNT- number at creation — the
  production-order precedent).

CROSS-MODULE IDS ARE OPAQUE (D-029/§5). ``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id
(nullable, validated via finance/queries when set — never a cross-module FK). ``assigned_to`` is a
core users id kept as a plain id (the journal posted_by precedent — no FK). The ``equipment_id`` /
``maintenance_plan_id`` links are INTRA-module composite tenant FKs.

Money columns use the D-015 MoneyType (scale-6, exact on both engines); a plain ``sa.Numeric`` would
round-trip through float on SQLite and lose precision (D-015), so it is never used for a stored
amount here.
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
from app.core.models import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    TenantMixin,
    TimestampMixin,
    UuidPKMixin,
    tenant_fk,
    tenant_unique,
)
from app.core.money import MoneyType
from app.modules.maintenance.constants import (
    EquipmentStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderType,
    MaintenancePlanStatus,
    IntervalUnit,
)


class Equipment(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """A piece of EQUIPMENT in the flat register (D-051): a machine, vehicle or asset maintenance is
    performed on.

    ``code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant (the master-data precedent — no auto-number).
    ``status`` runs the ``EquipmentStatus`` lifecycle. ``location`` is a FREE-TEXT label (e.g. "Plant
    A / Line 3") — NOT a functional-location hierarchy (that is out of v1, D-051).
    ``manufacturer`` / ``model`` / ``serial_number`` carry the nameplate data; ``commissioned_date``
    is when it entered service. ``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id (nullable,
    validated via finance/queries when set — for cost attribution). Audited (D-010): master data
    driving maintenance.
    """

    __tablename__ = "pm_equipment"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_pm_equipment_tenant_id_code"),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        # The (tenant, code) UNIQUE already serves the code lookup; this index serves the filtered
        # status list (PERFORMANCE §1).
        sa.Index("ix_pm_equipment_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
    )

    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=EquipmentStatus.ACTIVE.value,
        server_default="ACTIVE",
    )
    # Free-text location label (D-051): NOT a functional-location hierarchy (out of v1 scope).
    location: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
    manufacturer: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
    model: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
    serial_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
    commissioned_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
    # Opaque finance cost-centre id (D-029): no cross-module FK; the service validates it via
    # finance/queries when set. For cost attribution of the equipment's maintenance.
    cost_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)


class MaintenancePlan(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """An interval-based PREVENTIVE maintenance PLAN (D-051): a recurring task on a piece of
    equipment.

    ``code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant. ``equipment_id`` is the INTRA-module composite
    tenant FK to the equipment the plan maintains. ``status`` runs the ``MaintenancePlanStatus``
    lifecycle. ``interval_value`` × ``interval_unit`` is the recurrence (e.g. every 3 MONTHS).
    ``task_description`` is the free-text work the generated orders carry. ``last_generated_date`` is
    the ``scheduled_date`` of the LAST order this plan generated (NULL until the first generation);
    ``next_due_date`` is when the NEXT order is due — the generation run creates an order when
    ``next_due_date <= as_of`` and advances it (the OVERDUE-ADVANCE rule: a plan overdue by multiple
    intervals generates ONE order and advances to the next FUTURE due date, D-051). ``estimated_cost``
    seeds the generated orders' estimate (nullable).

    Mixes in DocumentMixin so the plan is a docflow PREDECESSOR of the orders its run generates
    (plan→'generates'→order). Audited (D-010): master data driving order generation.
    """

    __tablename__ = "pm_maintenance_plans"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_pm_maintenance_plans_tenant_id_code"),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("pm_equipment", "equipment_id"),
        document_fk(),
        sa.CheckConstraint(
            "interval_value > 0", name="ck_pm_maintenance_plans_interval_positive"
        ),
        # The generation run scans ACTIVE plans due on/before a date (PERFORMANCE §1): the composite
        # serves the set-based due-plan scan.
        sa.Index(
            "ix_pm_maintenance_plans_tenant_id_status_next_due_date",
            "tenant_id",
            "status",
            "next_due_date",
        ),
        sa.Index(
            "ix_pm_maintenance_plans_tenant_id_equipment_id",
            "tenant_id",
            "equipment_id",
        ),
    )

    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
    # INTRA-module composite tenant FK to pm_equipment.
    equipment_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=MaintenancePlanStatus.ACTIVE.value,
        server_default="ACTIVE",
    )
    interval_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
    interval_unit: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(10), nullable=False)
    task_description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=False)
    last_generated_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
    next_due_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
    estimated_cost: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=True)


class MaintenanceOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """A MAINTENANCE ORDER header (D-051): the order to maintain a piece of equipment.

    ``order_number`` is the gapless MNT- number claimed at creation. ``order_type`` is CORRECTIVE
    (ad-hoc) or PREVENTIVE (generated by a plan). ``status`` runs the ``MaintenanceOrderStatus``
    lifecycle. ``equipment_id`` is the INTRA-module composite tenant FK to the equipment;
    ``maintenance_plan_id`` (nullable) is set when a plan's run generated this order (a CORRECTIVE
    order has none). ``description`` is the free-text work. ``scheduled_date`` is the planned date;
    ``completed_date`` is stamped at completion. ``estimated_cost`` / ``actual_cost`` are MoneyType
    (the actual recorded at completion — record-only, no GL posting, D-051). ``assigned_to`` is the
    technician's user id (a plain id, no FK — the journal posted_by precedent).

    Registers a document + claims the gapless MNT- number at creation (D-012). Audited (D-010): a
    maintenance order tracks cost.
    """

    __tablename__ = "pm_maintenance_orders"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("pm_equipment", "equipment_id"),
        tenant_fk("pm_maintenance_plans", "maintenance_plan_id"),
        document_fk(),
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "order_number",
            name="uq_pm_maintenance_orders_tenant_id_order_number",
        ),
        # The list filters on (tenant, equipment, status) and (tenant, status, scheduled_date)
        # (PERFORMANCE §1): the equipment's open orders + the scheduled-date worklist.
        sa.Index(
            "ix_pm_maintenance_orders_tenant_id_equipment_id_status",
            "tenant_id",
            "equipment_id",
            "status",
        ),
        sa.Index(
            "ix_pm_maintenance_orders_tenant_id_status_scheduled_date",
            "tenant_id",
            "status",
            "scheduled_date",
        ),
    )

    order_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
    order_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=MaintenanceOrderType.CORRECTIVE.value,
        server_default="CORRECTIVE",
    )
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=MaintenanceOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
        server_default="DRAFT",
    )
    # INTRA-module composite tenant FK to pm_equipment.
    equipment_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    # INTRA-module composite tenant FK to pm_maintenance_plans (nullable — set when generated by a
    # preventive plan's run; a corrective order has none).
    maintenance_plan_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=False)
    scheduled_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
    completed_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
    estimated_cost: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=True)
    # Recorded at completion (record-only — no GL posting in v1, D-051).
    actual_cost: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=True)
    # The assigned technician (a core users id, kept as a plain id like a journal's posted_by — no
    # FK).
    assigned_to: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)

"""Maintenance request/response schemas (Pydantic v2, ApiModel base) for PLAN 9.2.

Create/Update/Read/Filter for the three entities (Equipment, MaintenanceOrder, MaintenancePlan) plus
the order action payloads (schedule / complete / cancel via path only) and the preventive run. Money
amounts are ``Decimal`` strings (D-015); a ``code`` is immutable so it is absent from the Update
schemas (the work-centre precedent). The Read schemas carry the server-derived fields (number,
status, computed next_due_date, timestamps).
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal

from app.core.schemas import ApiModel
from app.modules.maintenance.constants import (
    EquipmentStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderType,
    MaintenancePlanStatus,
    IntervalUnit,
)


# --- Equipment ----------------------------------------------------------------


class EquipmentCreate(ApiModel):
    """Create a piece of equipment. ``code`` is user-supplied + unique per tenant; ``cost_center_id``
    (optional) is validated to exist in finance when set (D-029)."""

    code: str
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    status: EquipmentStatus = EquipmentStatus.ACTIVE
    location: str | None = None
    manufacturer: str | None = None
    model: str | None = None
    serial_number: str | None = None
    commissioned_date: date | None = None
    cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    notes: str | None = None


class EquipmentUpdate(ApiModel):
    """Partial update. ``code`` is immutable (absent here); a changed ``cost_center_id`` is
    re-validated. All fields optional — only the set ones change (exclude_unset)."""

    name: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    status: EquipmentStatus | None = None
    location: str | None = None
    manufacturer: str | None = None
    model: str | None = None
    serial_number: str | None = None
    commissioned_date: date | None = None
    cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    notes: str | None = None


class EquipmentRead(ApiModel):
    id: uuid.UUID
    code: str
    name: str
    description: str | None
    status: EquipmentStatus
    location: str | None
    manufacturer: str | None
    model: str | None
    serial_number: str | None
    commissioned_date: date | None
    cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None
    notes: str | None
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime


class EquipmentFilter(ApiModel):
    """List filters. None means "no constraint"; folded into the cursor's filter fingerprint so a
    cursor cannot cross filtered views."""

    status: EquipmentStatus | None = None


# --- Maintenance order --------------------------------------------------------


class MaintenanceOrderCreate(ApiModel):
    """Create a CORRECTIVE maintenance order (ad-hoc). The equipment must exist and be ACTIVE.
    ``scheduled_date`` makes it SCHEDULED at creation; omitting it leaves it DRAFT. PREVENTIVE orders
    are NOT created via this schema — they come from a plan's run. ``order_type`` is therefore not a
    field (always CORRECTIVE here)."""

    equipment_id: uuid.UUID
    description: str
    scheduled_date: date | None = None
    estimated_cost: Decimal | None = None
    assigned_to: uuid.UUID | None = None
    notes: str | None = None


class MaintenanceOrderUpdate(ApiModel):

"""Maintenance's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5 / D-051).

Maintenance sits ABOVE finance in the dependency order; nothing imports this yet (it is the newest
module), but it is the ONLY maintenance file a later module may import — kept thin and stable. The
service and router use these reads too. Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under
the caller's tenant context, so the D-007 filter applies on top — ordinary tenant-scoped reads.

``due_plans`` is the SET-BASED scan the preventive-generation run drives (PERFORMANCE §2): one query
returns every ACTIVE plan due on/before ``as_of``, ordered by code for a deterministic generation
order — no per-plan N+1 in the run beyond the order creation.
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.modules.maintenance.constants import MaintenancePlanStatus
from app.modules.maintenance.models import Equipment, MaintenanceOrder, MaintenancePlan


async def get_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, equipment_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Equipment | None:
    """The equipment with ``equipment_id`` in the tenant, or None. A point lookup on the PK."""
    stmt = select(Equipment).where(
        Equipment.tenant_id == tenant_id, Equipment.id == equipment_id
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def equipment_exists(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, equipment_id: uuid.UUID
) -> bool:
    """Whether a piece of equipment with ``equipment_id`` exists in the tenant (a cheap id probe the
    plan/order create paths use)."""
    stmt = select(Equipment.id).where(
        Equipment.tenant_id == tenant_id, Equipment.id == equipment_id
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None


async def get_maintenance_order(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MaintenanceOrder | None:
    """The maintenance order with ``order_id`` in the tenant, or None. A point lookup on the PK."""
    stmt = select(MaintenanceOrder).where(
        MaintenanceOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id, MaintenanceOrder.id == order_id
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def orders_for_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, equipment_id: uuid.UUID
) -> list[MaintenanceOrder]:
    """The maintenance orders raised against one piece of equipment (D-051), ordered by order_number.
    The set an equipment detail / history view reads. Index-served by (tenant, equipment_id,
    status)."""
    stmt = (
        select(MaintenanceOrder)
        .where(
            MaintenanceOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            MaintenanceOrder.equipment_id == equipment_id,
        )
        .order_by(MaintenanceOrder.order_number)
    )
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())


async def get_maintenance_plan(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, plan_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MaintenancePlan | None:
    """The maintenance plan with ``plan_id`` in the tenant, or None. A point lookup on the PK."""
    stmt = select(MaintenancePlan).where(
        MaintenancePlan.tenant_id == tenant_id, MaintenancePlan.id == plan_id
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def due_plans(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, as_of: date
) -> list[MaintenancePlan]:
    """Every ACTIVE maintenance plan due on/before ``as_of`` (D-051) — the SET-BASED scan the
    preventive-generation run drives (PERFORMANCE §2: ONE query, no per-plan N+1). Ordered by code so
    the generation order is deterministic. Index-served by (tenant, status, next_due_date)."""
    stmt = (
        select(MaintenancePlan)
        .where(
            MaintenancePlan.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            MaintenancePlan.status == MaintenancePlanStatus.ACTIVE.value,
            MaintenancePlan.next_due_date <= as_of,
        )
        .order_by(MaintenancePlan.code)
    )
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())

"""Equipment business logic (PLAN 9.2, D-051): CRUD + cost-centre validation.

The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin. The optional
``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id (D-029): validated to exist via
``finance/queries.cost_center_exists`` (the sanctioned cross-module read, STRUCTURE §5) — never a
cross-module FK. ``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[Equipment]`` (the ORM model) a
string at import; the router re-validates page items.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
from app.core.schemas import Page
from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
from app.modules.maintenance.models import Equipment
from app.modules.maintenance.schemas import (
    EquipmentCreate,
    EquipmentFilter,
    EquipmentUpdate,
)


async def _validate_cost_center(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None
) -> None:
    """A supplied cost-centre id must exist in finance (D-029): validated via the finance queries
    contract, never a cross-module FK. None is skipped (the cost centre is optional)."""
    if cost_center_id is None:
        return
    if not await finance_queries.cost_center_exists(session, tenant_id, cost_center_id):
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="Referenced cost centre does not exist",
            code="maintenance.cost_center_not_found",
            details={"cost_center_id": str(cost_center_id)},
        )


async def get_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, equipment_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Equipment:
    equipment = await session.get(Equipment, equipment_id)
    if equipment is None or equipment.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(
            message="Equipment not found", code="maintenance.equipment_not_found"
        )
    return equipment


async def create_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: EquipmentCreate
) -> Equipment:
    """Create a piece of equipment. Rejects a duplicate code (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop);
    validates the cost centre exists in finance when set."""
    existing = (
        await session.execute(
            select(Equipment.id).where(
                Equipment.tenant_id == tenant_id, Equipment.code == payload.code
            )
        )
    ).first()
    if existing is not None:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"Equipment with code {payload.code} already exists",
            code="maintenance.equipment_code_conflict",
            details={"code": payload.code},
        )
    await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, payload.cost_center_id)
    equipment = Equipment(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        code=payload.code,
        name=payload.name,
        description=payload.description,
        status=payload.status.value,
        location=payload.location,
        manufacturer=payload.manufacturer,
        model=payload.model,
        serial_number=payload.serial_number,
        commissioned_date=payload.commissioned_date,
        cost_center_id=payload.cost_center_id,
        notes=payload.notes,
    )
    session.add(equipment)
    await session.flush()
    return equipment


async def update_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    equipment_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: EquipmentUpdate,
) -> Equipment:
    """Partial update (D-010: mutate the loaded object so the audit diff is captured). ``code`` is
    immutable and absent from the schema; a changed cost centre is re-validated; an enum value is
    stored as its string."""
    equipment = await get_equipment(session, tenant_id, equipment_id)
    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    if "cost_center_id" in data:
        await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, data["cost_center_id"])
    if data.get("status") is not None:
        data["status"] = data["status"].value
    for field, value in data.items():
        setattr(equipment, field, value)
    await session.flush()
    return equipment


async def list_equipment(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    filters: EquipmentFilter,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
) -> Page[Equipment]:
    """Keyset-paginated equipment ordered by code (D-014). The status filter narrows the set
    (index-served by (tenant, status)) and folds into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot
    bleed across views."""
    stmt = select(Equipment).where(Equipment.tenant_id == tenant_id)
    if filters.status is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(Equipment.status == filters.status.value)
    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(filters.status)
    return await paginate(
        session,
        stmt,
        order_by=[OrderKey(Equipment.code, SortDirection.ASC)],
        pk=Equipment.id,
        cursor=cursor,
        limit=limit,
        filters=fingerprint,
    )

"""Maintenance-order lifecycle (PLAN 9.2, D-051): create corrective, schedule / start / complete /
cancel + reads.

A CORRECTIVE order is created ad-hoc against ACTIVE equipment; a PREVENTIVE order is generated by a
plan's run (in plans.py, which calls ``create_generated_order`` here). Both register a document and
claim the gapless MNT- number at creation (the production-order precedent). COMPLETE records the
``actual_cost`` ON THE ORDER (record-only — no GL posting in v1, D-051: the parity scope is
"corrective/preventive orders", not full work-order costing; a GL posting through the cost centre is
a documented later).

``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[MaintenanceOrder]`` a string at import.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import date

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core import docflow
from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
from app.core.schemas import Page
from app.modules.maintenance.constants import (
    MAINTENANCE_ORDER_DOC_TYPE,
    MAINTENANCE_ORDER_NUMBER_PADDING,
    MAINTENANCE_ORDER_NUMBER_PREFIX,
    MAINTENANCE_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME,
    EquipmentStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderStatus,
    MaintenanceOrderType,
)
from app.modules.maintenance.models import MaintenanceOrder
from app.modules.maintenance.schemas import (
    CompleteOrderRequest,
    MaintenanceOrderCreate,
    MaintenanceOrderUpdate,
)
from app.modules.maintenance.service.equipment import get_equipment

# Statuses an order can no longer be edited/scheduled/started/cancelled from (terminal).
_TERMINAL = (MaintenanceOrderStatus.COMPLETED, MaintenanceOrderStatus.CANCELLED)


async def get_maintenance_order(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    order = await session.get(MaintenanceOrder, order_id)
    if order is None or order.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(
            message="Maintenance order not found",
            code="maintenance.order_not_found",
        )
    return order


async def _claim_order_number(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
) -> str:
    """Ensure the MNT- sequence exists for the tenant and claim the next gapless number (D-012)."""
    await ensure_sequence(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME,
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_NUMBER_PREFIX,
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_NUMBER_PADDING,
        year_reset=True,
    )
    return await claim_number(
        session, tenant_id, MAINTENANCE_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=on_date
    )


async def _insert_order(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    order_type: MaintenanceOrderType,
    status: MaintenanceOrderStatus,
    equipment_id: uuid.UUID,
    description: str,
    scheduled_date: date,
    maintenance_plan_id: uuid.UUID | None,
    estimated_cost,
    assigned_to: uuid.UUID | None,
    notes: str | None,
    on_date: date,
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Register the order document, claim its gapless MNT- number, persist the order row (D-012). The
    shared insert behind both the corrective create and the plan-generated create."""
    order_id = uuid.uuid4()
    document = await docflow.register_document(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        MAINTENANCE_ORDER_DOC_TYPE,
        order_id,
        doc_number=None,
        status=status.value,
    )
    number = await _claim_order_number(session, tenant_id, on_date)
    order = MaintenanceOrder(
        id=order_id,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        document_id=document.id,
        order_number=number,
        order_type=order_type.value,
        status=status.value,
        equipment_id=equipment_id,
        maintenance_plan_id=maintenance_plan_id,
        description=description,
        scheduled_date=scheduled_date,
        estimated_cost=estimated_cost,
        assigned_to=assigned_to,
        notes=notes,
    )
    session.add(order)
    await session.flush()
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=number, status=status.value
    )
    return order


async def create_corrective(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: MaintenanceOrderCreate
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Create a CORRECTIVE maintenance order ad-hoc (D-051). The equipment must exist AND be ACTIVE
    (a maintenance order targets equipment in service — an INACTIVE/RETIRED unit is rejected 422).
    Born SCHEDULED when a ``scheduled_date`` is given, else DRAFT (it is scheduled later via the
    action). Registers the document + claims the MNT- number."""
    equipment = await get_equipment(session, tenant_id, payload.equipment_id)
    if EquipmentStatus(equipment.status) != EquipmentStatus.ACTIVE:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="A maintenance order can only target ACTIVE equipment",
            code="maintenance.equipment_not_active",
            details={"equipment_id": str(payload.equipment_id), "status": equipment.status},
        )
    scheduled = payload.scheduled_date
    status = (
        MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED
        if scheduled is not None
        else MaintenanceOrderStatus.DRAFT
    )
    return await _insert_order(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        order_type=MaintenanceOrderType.CORRECTIVE,
        status=status,
        equipment_id=payload.equipment_id,
        description=payload.description,
        # A DRAFT order still needs a scheduled_date column value (NOT NULL); default it to today
        # until the schedule action sets the real planned date.
        scheduled_date=scheduled if scheduled is not None else date.today(),
        maintenance_plan_id=None,
        estimated_cost=payload.estimated_cost,
        assigned_to=payload.assigned_to,
        notes=payload.notes,
        on_date=date.today(),
    )


async def create_generated_order(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    equipment_id: uuid.UUID,
    maintenance_plan_id: uuid.UUID,
    description: str,
    scheduled_date: date,
    estimated_cost,
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Create a PREVENTIVE order from a plan's run (D-051) — born SCHEDULED at the plan's due date,
    linked to the plan. Called by plans.run_preventive_maintenance; the plan→order docflow edge is
    written by the caller (it owns the plan document)."""
    return await _insert_order(
        session,
        tenant_id,
        order_type=MaintenanceOrderType.PREVENTIVE,
        status=MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED,
        equipment_id=equipment_id,
        description=description,
        scheduled_date=scheduled_date,
        maintenance_plan_id=maintenance_plan_id,
        estimated_cost=estimated_cost,
        assigned_to=None,
        notes=None,
        on_date=scheduled_date,
    )


async def update_order(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    order_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: MaintenanceOrderUpdate,
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Partial update of a non-terminal order's editable fields (D-010: mutate the loaded object).
    A COMPLETED/CANCELLED order is immutable (409)."""
    order = await get_maintenance_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
    if MaintenanceOrderStatus(order.status) in _TERMINAL:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A {order.status} maintenance order cannot be edited",
            code="maintenance.order_terminal",
            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
        )
    for field, value in payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True).items():
        setattr(order, field, value)
    await session.flush()
    return order


async def _transition(
    session: AsyncSession,
    order: MaintenanceOrder,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    new_status: MaintenanceOrderStatus,
) -> None:
    """Set the order + its registry document to ``new_status`` in the owning transaction."""
    order.status = new_status.value
    await session.flush()
    await docflow.set_document_status(
        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=new_status.value
    )


async def schedule_order(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    order_id: uuid.UUID,
    scheduled_date: date,
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Schedule a DRAFT order (D-051): DRAFT → SCHEDULED with the planned date. An already-SCHEDULED
    order may be re-scheduled (the date is updated, status unchanged). A started/terminal order
    cannot be scheduled (409)."""
    order = await get_maintenance_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
    status = MaintenanceOrderStatus(order.status)
    if status not in (MaintenanceOrderStatus.DRAFT, MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED):
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A {order.status} maintenance order cannot be scheduled",
            code="maintenance.order_not_schedulable",
            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
        )
    order.scheduled_date = scheduled_date
    if status == MaintenanceOrderStatus.DRAFT:
        await _transition(session, order, tenant_id, MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED)
    else:
        await session.flush()
    return order


async def start_order(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Start work on a SCHEDULED order (D-051): SCHEDULED → IN_PROGRESS. A DRAFT order must be
    scheduled first; a started/terminal order cannot be started again (409)."""
    order = await get_maintenance_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
    if MaintenanceOrderStatus(order.status) != MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A {order.status} maintenance order cannot be started",
            code="maintenance.order_not_startable",
            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
        )
    await _transition(session, order, tenant_id, MaintenanceOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS)
    return order


async def complete_order(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    order_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: CompleteOrderRequest,
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Complete an order (D-051): SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED, recording ``actual_cost`` and the
    completion date (record-only — no GL posting in v1; the cost lives on the order, D-051). A
    DRAFT/terminal order cannot be completed (409)."""
    order = await get_maintenance_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
    status = MaintenanceOrderStatus(order.status)
    if status not in (
        MaintenanceOrderStatus.SCHEDULED,
        MaintenanceOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A {order.status} maintenance order cannot be completed",
            code="maintenance.order_not_completable",
            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
        )
    order.actual_cost = payload.actual_cost
    order.completed_date = payload.completed_date or date.today()
    await _transition(session, order, tenant_id, MaintenanceOrderStatus.COMPLETED)
    return order


async def cancel_order(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MaintenanceOrder:
    """Cancel a non-terminal order (D-051): DRAFT/SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED. A
    COMPLETED/CANCELLED order is terminal (409)."""
    order = await get_maintenance_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
    if MaintenanceOrderStatus(order.status) in _TERMINAL:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A {order.status} maintenance order cannot be cancelled",
            code="maintenance.order_not_cancellable",
            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
        )
    await _transition(session, order, tenant_id, MaintenanceOrderStatus.CANCELLED)
    return order


async def list_maintenance_orders(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    equipment_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
    order_type: MaintenanceOrderType | None = None,
    status: MaintenanceOrderStatus | None = None,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
) -> Page[MaintenanceOrder]:
    """Keyset-paginated maintenance orders ordered by order_number (D-014). The
    equipment/type/status filters narrow the set (index-served by (tenant, equipment, status) /
    (tenant, status, scheduled_date)) and fold into the cursor fingerprint."""
    stmt = select(MaintenanceOrder).where(MaintenanceOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id)
    if equipment_id is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(MaintenanceOrder.equipment_id == equipment_id)
    if order_type is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(MaintenanceOrder.order_type == order_type.value)
    if status is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(MaintenanceOrder.status == status.value)
    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(equipment_id, order_type, status)
    return await paginate(
        session,
        stmt,
        order_by=[OrderKey(MaintenanceOrder.order_number, SortDirection.ASC)],
        pk=MaintenanceOrder.id,
        cursor=cursor,
        limit=limit,
        filters=fingerprint,
    )
